sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface
translations.idiomatic: Preface

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝有言：「百姓所以安其田里而無歎息愁恨之心者，政平訟理也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han had a saying: 'The reason the common people can rest secure in their fields and lanes without sighing in resentment is that government is evenhanded and lawsuits are fairly judged.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han once said that people live quietly in their villages without bitter complaint when governance is fair and justice runs true.

sentences.zh: 與我共此者，其唯良二千石乎！

translations.literal: Those who share this with me—are they not only the good commandery governors [at two thousand shi]?'
translations.idiomatic: Only sound prefects—those who truly earn their two-thousand-bushel salary—share that achievement with the throne.'

sentences.zh: 」此則長吏之官，實為撫導之本。

translations.literal: This shows that the office of senior magistrate is truly the root of comforting and guiding the people.
translations.idiomatic: In other words, the county-level chief is the foundation of good rule and sound guidance.

sentences.zh: 是以東裏相鄭，西門宰鄴，潁川黃霸，蜀郡文翁，或吏不敢欺，或人懷其惠，或教移齊魯，或政務寬和，斯並惇史播其徽音，良能以為准的。

translations.literal: Therefore Dongli Zichan as minister of Zheng, Ximen Bao as magistrate of Ye, Huang Ba of Yingchuan, Wen Weng of Shu commandery—some caused clerks not to dare deceive them, some caused the people to cherish their kindness, some carried instruction into Qi and Lu, some administered affairs with lenience and harmony; these were all proclaimed by earnest historians and taken as standards by able men.
translations.idiomatic: From Zi Chan in Zheng and Ximen Bao in Ye to Huang Ba in Yingchuan and Wen Weng in Shu—some overawed corrupt clerks, some won deep affection, some spread Confucian reform through Qi and Lu, some ruled with calm kindness—history praised them, and capable officials ever since have taken them as their yardstick.

sentences.zh: 有晉肇茲王業，光啟霸圖，授方任能，經文緯武。

translations.literal: When Jin founded its royal enterprise here and opened wide its hegemonic design, it assigned regions and employed worthies, ordering the civil realm and arraying the martial.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house raised its kingship and unfurled ambition across the realm, putting the right men in the right posts and pairing civil order with military strength.

sentences.zh: 泰始受禪，改物君臨，纂三葉之鴻基，膺百王之大寶，勞心庶績，垂意黎元，申敕守宰之司，婁發憂矜之詔，辭旨懇切，誨諭殷勤，欲使直道正身，抑末敦本。

translations.literal: At Taishi, receiving the abdication and changing the mandate to rule as sovereign, inheriting the vast foundation of three reigns and receiving the great treasure passed down through a hundred kings, laboring over the myriad tasks of government and turning attention to the common people, repeatedly charging those who guarded and governed districts and issuing again and again edicts of anxious sympathy—wording earnest and urgent, instruction diligent—wishing to make officials walk the straight path and correct themselves, restraining the secondary and strengthening the root.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taishi accession onward the throne changed hands peacefully; the dynasty inherited three generations of accumulated power and the nominal legitimacy of a long line of kings, toiled at every branch of administration, looked after the commoners, lectured prefects and magistrates again and again, and issued repeated edicts of heartfelt concern—demanding integrity, discipline, and a return to fundamental virtues.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，可謂農安其業，吏盡其能者歟！

translations.literal: In such an hour, could one not say that farmers were secure in their occupations and clerks fulfilled their duties?
translations.idiomatic: At that moment it seemed farmers could stay at their plows and officials actually did their jobs.

sentences.zh: 而帝寬厚足以君人，明威未能厲俗，政刑以之私謁，賄賂於此公行，結綬者以放濁為通，彈冠者以苟得為貴，流遁忘反，浸以為常。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's generous tolerance sufficed to rule men as lord, but his awesome clarity could not steel custom; government and punishments were bent by private soliciting, bribes ran openly here; those who tied their seals took looseness and corruption as 'getting through,' those who brushed caps took grasping gain as honor; drift and escape became forgetfulness of return, gradually entrenched as normal.
translations.idiomatic: But imperial lenience let him govern without inspiring awe; customs did not stiffen. Justice bent to pull and patronage; gifts passed hands in broad daylight. Men who wore official cords treated laxity and graft as sophistication; men who entered office prized whatever they could grab. People slid away and forgot to return until vice passed for routine.

sentences.zh: 劉毅抗賣官之言，當時以為矯枉，察其風俗，豈虛也哉！

translations.literal: Liu Yi spoke out against selling offices—people of the time thought him excessive in correcting a fault; observe the customs—was it empty talk?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi denounced the sale of offices, contemporaries called his remedy overwrought—yet look at how morals actually behaved, and his warning rings true.

sentences.zh: 爰及惠懷，中州鼎沸，逮于江左，晉政多門，元帝比少康之隆，處仲為梗，海西微昌邑之罪，元子亂常，既權逼是憂，故羈縻成俗。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Hui and Emperor Huai, the Central Plain boiled like a cauldron; down to the left bank of the Yangzi, Jin policy had many doors. The Yuan Emperor compared himself to the prosperity of Shao Kang, but Wang Dun was an obstruction; the Prince of Haixi raised King Changyi of Han's faults on a small scale, and Huan Wen disturbed the norm; once power and coercion became the worry, lax restraint hardened into custom.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hui and Huai the heartland exploded into chaos; after the court crossed to the south, authority fractured among factions. Emperor Yuan likened his restoration to Shao Kang's revival, yet Wang Dun blocked him; the deposed emperor at Haixi echoed King Changyi's scandal on a lesser scale, and Huan Wen upset the proper order. Fear of raw coercion turned indulgence into habit.

sentences.zh: 蒞職者為身擇利，銓綜者為人擇官，下僚多英俊之才，勢位必高門之胄，遂使良能之績僅有存焉。

translations.literal: Those who took office chose profit for themselves; those who handled appointments chose posts for others; subordinates were often men of outstanding talent, but powerful positions inevitably went to sons of eminent houses—so that the achievements of the truly able survived only in scattered instances.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders picked rewards for themselves; personnel clerks picked jobs for friends. Staff might be brilliant, yet real power stayed with great-clan heirs, so genuine administrative talent surfaced only here and there.

sentences.zh: 雖復茂弘以明允贊經綸，安石以時宗鎮雅俗，然外虞孔熾，內難方殷，而匡救彌縫，方免傾覆，弘風革弊，彼則未遑。

translations.literal: Although again Wang Dao with enlightened fairness assisted in ordering the realm, and Xie An as pillar of the age steadied refined custom, still outer alarms blazed fiercely and inner troubles ran deep; patching and mending barely averted collapse—there was no leisure to spread transforming influence and reform abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao lent steady judgment to statecraft and Xie An anchored elite opinion, but foreign crises flared and domestic strife seethed; they spent every ounce of energy merely preventing collapse, with no room left to reform manners root and branch.

sentences.zh: 今采其政績可稱者，以為《良吏傳》。

translations.literal: Now I select those whose administrative records deserve praise and make of them the 'Biographies of Good Officials.'
translations.idiomatic: This chapter gathers officials whose deeds on the job merit remembrance—the Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 魯芝

translations.literal: Lu Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi

sentences.zh: 魯芝，字世英，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Shiying, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi (courtesy Shiying) came from Mei county in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 世有名德，為西州豪族。

translations.literal: For generations his family had enjoyed renowned virtue and was a powerful clan of the western provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long been celebrated for integrity and ranked among the great houses of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 父為郭氾所害，芝繈褓流離，年十七，乃移居雍，耽思墳籍。

translations.literal: His father was killed by Guo Si; Zhi, still in swaddling clothes, wandered destitute, and at seventeen he moved to Yong, immersing himself in study of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Si murdered his father; Zhi was still an infant when the family was scattered. At seventeen he settled in Yong and buried himself in the canon.

sentences.zh: 郡舉上計吏，州辟別駕。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as clerk for the annual accounting; the province summoned him as provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him accounts clerk; the province called him up as provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 魏車騎將軍郭淮為雍州刺史，深敬重之。

translations.literal: Guo Huai, General of Chariots and Cavalry of Wei, was Inspector of Yong Province and held him in deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: Wei general Guo Huai, as inspector of Yong, treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中。

translations.literal: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed gentleman of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he received a gentleman-of-the-interior appointment.

sentences.zh: 會蜀相諸葛亮侵隴右，淮復請芝為別駕。

translations.literal: When the Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang invaded Longyou, Huai again asked Zhi to serve as provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang of Shu struck Longyou, Guo Huai again kept him on as provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 事平，薦於公府，辟大司馬曹真掾，轉臨淄侯文學。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, [Zhi] was recommended to the ministerial offices and summoned as aide to the Grand Marshal Cao Zhen; he was transferred to literary instructor to the Marquis of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: After hostilities ended he went to the central ministries, served as staff to Grand Marshal Cao Zhen, then moved to tutor of literature for the marquis of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 鄭袤薦于司空王朗，朗即加禮命。

translations.literal: Zheng Mao recommended him to Minister of Works Wang Lang, and Lang at once treated him with courtesy and appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mao introduced him to Wang Lang, minister of works, who honored him with an immediate posting.

sentences.zh: 後拜騎都尉、參軍事、行安南太守，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, joined military affairs, acted as Administrator of An'nan, was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Commandant of Cavalry, military adviser, acting administrator of An'nan, and gentleman at the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曹真出督關右，又參大司馬軍事。

translations.literal: When Cao Zhen went out to supervise the west of the Pass, [Zhi] again joined the Grand Marshal's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Zhen supervised the region west of the passes, Zhi again served on the grand marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 真薨，宣帝代焉，乃引芝參驃騎軍事，轉天水太守。

translations.literal: When Zhen died, the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] replaced him and then brought Zhi in to join the military staff of the General of Agile Cavalry; [Zhi] was transferred to Administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Zhen died Sima Yi took his place and attached Zhi to the agile-cavalry command; Zhi then became administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 郡鄰於蜀，數被侵掠，戶口減削，寇盜充斥，芝傾心鎮衛，更造城市，數年間舊境悉復。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered Shu and repeatedly suffered invasion and plunder; households dwindled and bandits swarmed. Zhi devoted himself to guarding and defending, rebuilt the walls and town, and within a few years the former territory was fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui lay against Shu and suffered repeated raids: population fell and bandits multiplied. Zhi threw himself into defense, rebuilt the city, and within a few years the district recovered its old bounds.

sentences.zh: 遷廣平太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangping.

sentences.zh: 天水夷夏慕德，老幼赴闕獻書，乞留芝。

translations.literal: Both Yi and Han Chinese in Tianshui admired his virtue; old and young went to the capital to submit petitions asking that Zhi be kept [in office].
translations.idiomatic: Yi tribesmen and Han alike cherished him; young and old traveled to the capital with petitions begging the court to keep him.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝許焉，仍策書嘉歎，勉以黃霸之美，加討寇將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was promoted to General Who Suppresses Brigands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming agreed, issued a warm commendation comparing him to Huang Ba, and added the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.

sentences.zh: 曹爽輔政，引為司馬。

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang dominated the government, [Shuang] brought [Zhi] in as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang controlled the regency he took Zhi on as marshal.

sentences.zh: 芝屢有讜言嘉謀，爽弗能納。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly offered forthright counsel and fine plans, which Shuang could not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi gave blunt, sound advice again and again; Shuang refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝起兵誅爽，芝率餘眾犯門斬關，馳出赴爽，勸爽曰：「公居伊周之位，一旦以罪見黜，雖欲牽黃犬，復可得乎！

translations.literal: When the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] raised troops to execute Shuang, Zhi led the remaining troops to force the gates and break through the barriers, galloping out to join Shuang, and urged Shuang: 'You occupy the position of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—once you are dismissed for crime, even if you wished to lead a yellow dog [on a hunt], could you have it again?
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi rose to purge Cao Shuang, Zhi rallied what troops he could, broke through the gates, and rode to Shuang's side, urging him: 'You stand in the place of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—if you lose office as a criminal, not even the fantasy of walking your yellow dog will be yours.

sentences.zh: 若挾天子保許昌，杖大威以羽檄征四方兵，孰敢不從！

translations.literal: If you seize the Son of Heaven and hold Xuchang, wielding great awe and dispatching feathered summons to levy troops from the four quarters, who would dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Seize the emperor, hold Xuchang, brandish imperial authority, and issue urgent summons to the provinces—who would refuse to march?'

sentences.zh: 舍此而去，欲就東市，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: To abandon this and depart, only to go to the eastern market [for execution]—how could it not be bitter?'
translations.idiomatic: Throw that chance away and march meekly to the execution ground—would that not be agony?'

sentences.zh: 」爽懦惑不能用，遂委身受戮。

translations.literal: Shuang was cowardly and confused and could not use [the advice]; he thereupon submitted his person and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was timid and bewildered and ignored him; he surrendered and died under the blade.

sentences.zh: 芝坐爽下獄，當死，而口不訟直，志不苟免。

translations.literal: Zhi, implicated under Shuang, was imprisoned and sentenced to death, yet he did not argue his innocence aloud and was resolved not to seek escape unworthily.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, tied to Shuang's faction, went to prison facing death, yet he neither whined for mercy nor grasped at an unworthy reprieve.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嘉之，赦而不誅。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xuan admired him and pardoned him without execution.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi admired him and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 俄而起為使持節、領護匈奴中郎將、振威將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed commissioner with credentials, concurrent Colonel for the Xiongnu of the Center, General Who Rouses Might, and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held credentials as commissioner, concurrent colonel of the central Xiongnu corps, General Who Rouses Might, and inspector of Bing.

sentences.zh: 以綏緝有方，遷大鴻臚。

translations.literal: For skilled pacification and administration he was promoted to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His skill at pacifying and administering won him promotion to grand herald.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公即位，賜爵關內侯，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang ascended the throne, [Zhi] was granted noble rank as secondary marquis within the passes, with an estate of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the duke of Gaoguixiang became emperor, Zhi received a secondary marquisate inside the passes with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉平，隨例增邑二百戶，拜揚武將軍、荆州刺史。

translations.literal: After Guanqiu Jian was pacified, by precedent his fief was increased by two hundred households; he was appointed General Who Displays Might and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanqiu Jian's rebellion was crushed his fief rose by another two hundred households by rule; he became General Who Displays Might and inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕以壽春叛，文帝奉魏帝出征，徵兵四方，芝率荊州文武以為先驅。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Dan rebelled at Shou-chun, Emperor Wen [Sima Zhao] led the Wei emperor on campaign, levying troops from the four quarters; Zhi led the civil and military officers of Jing Province as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan rose at Shou-chun, Sima Zhao marched with the Wei emperor and called troops from every quarter; Zhi led Jing's civil and military officers in the van.

sentences.zh: 誕平，進爵武進亭侯，又增邑九百戶。

translations.literal: When Dan was pacified, his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Wujin precinct, and another nine hundred households were added to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: After Dan fell he advanced to marquis of Wujin precinct with nine hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 遷大尚書，掌刑理。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Masters of Writing with expanded duties, in charge of penal administration.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Masters of Writing with broadened duties and oversaw penal justice.

sentences.zh: 常道鄉公即位，進爵斄城鄉侯，又增邑八百戶，遷監青州諸軍事、振武將軍、青州刺史，轉平東將軍。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Changdao Township ascended the throne, his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Lai Township, another eight hundred households were added to his fief, he was promoted to supervise military affairs in Qing Province with concurrent appointment as General Who Rouses Might and Inspector of Qing Province, and transferred to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: When the duke of Changdao succeeded, his title rose to marquis of Lai township with eight hundred more households; he supervised Qing military affairs as General Who Rouses Might and inspector of Qing, then shifted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封陰平伯。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new five-rank nobility he became baron of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，轉鎮東將軍，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, [Zhi] was transferred to General Who Guards the East and his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne Zhi became General Who Guards the East and full marquis.

sentences.zh: 帝以芝清忠履正，素無居宅，使軍兵為作屋五十間。

translations.literal: Because Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a dwelling, the emperor had soldiers build fifty rooms for him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his integrity and learning he still owned no house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.

sentences.zh: 芝以年及懸車，告老遜位，章表十餘上，於是徵為光祿大夫，位特進，給吏卒，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Zhi, feeling his years had reached the age to hang up his carriage [retire], requested retirement and yielded his position; memorials ran to more than ten submissions—whereupon he was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Household with nominal salary only, rank specially advanced, given clerks and soldiers, and a barrier gate was erected at his door.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling he had reached retiring age, he repeatedly memorialized to step down—more than ten times—until the court recalled him as minister of the imperial household at nominal salary with specially advanced rank, staff and guards, and the privilege of a barrier gate.

sentences.zh: 羊祜為車騎將軍，乃以位讓芝，曰：「光祿大夫魯芝潔身寡欲，和而不同，服事華髮，以禮終始，未蒙此選，臣更越之，何以塞天下之望！

translations.literal: Yang Hu was General of Chariots and Cavalry and wished to yield his position to Zhi, saying: 'Minister of the Imperial Household Lu Zhi keeps himself pure with few desires, harmonizes without agreeing blindly, has served until his hair is hoary and observes ritual from first to last—he has not yet received this selection; if I leap past him, how shall I answer the hopes of the realm?'
translations.idiomatic: General of chariots Yang Hu tried to give him the post, arguing that Lu Zhi lived modestly, harmonized without flattery, and had served honorably into old age without this promotion—'If I vault ahead of him, how do I face the empire?'

sentences.zh: 」上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 其為人所重如是。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which others held him.
translations.idiomatic: That was how highly peers valued him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 帝為舉哀，賵贈有加，諡曰貞，賜塋田百畝。

translations.literal: The emperor held mourning for him; burial gifts were augmented beyond the norm; his posthumous name was Zhen [Steadfast], and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned him, enriched his grave goods, gave the posthumous name Zhen ('steadfast'), and allotted one hundred mu of burial land.

sentences.zh: 胡威

translations.literal: Hu Wei
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei

sentences.zh: 胡威，字伯武，一名貔。

translations.literal: Hu Wei, courtesy name Bowu, also called Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei (courtesy Bowu), also known as Pi.

sentences.zh: 淮南壽春人也。

translations.literal: He was a native of Shou-chun in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Shou-chun in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 父質，以忠清著稱，少與鄉人蔣濟、硃績俱知名于江淮間，仕魏至征東將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was famed for loyalty and purity; in youth he was known together with fellow villagers Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji throughout the lands between the Jiang and Huai, and served Wei up to General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hu Zhi won fame for loyalty and rectitude; as a young man he stood alongside Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji from the same district across the Jiang-Huai region, rising in Wei to general who conquers the east and inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 威早厲志尚。

translations.literal: Wei from his youth cultivated aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wei shaped his ambitions early.

sentences.zh: 質之為荊州也，威自京都定省，家貧，無車馬僮僕，自驅驢單行。

translations.literal: When Zhi was Inspector of Jing Province, Wei came from the capital to visit his parents; the family was poor and had no carriage, horses, or servants—he drove a donkey alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Zhi governed Jing, Wei traveled from the capital to visit; the household was destitute—no cart, horses, or servants—so he rode a donkey by himself.

sentences.zh: 每至客舍，躬放驢，取樵炊爨，食畢，復隨侶進道。

translations.literal: Whenever he reached an inn, he personally tended the donkey, gathered firewood to cook and boil [his food], and after eating continued on the road with fellow travelers.
translations.idiomatic: At every hostel he watered his mount, gathered firewood, cooked his meal, ate, and moved on with other travelers.

sentences.zh: 既至，見父，停廄中十餘日。

translations.literal: When he arrived he saw his father and stayed in the stable more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his father he lodged in the stable over ten days.

sentences.zh: 告歸，父賜絹一匹為裝。

translations.literal: When he announced his departure, his father gave him one bolt of silk for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to leave, his father gave him one bolt of silk for the road.

sentences.zh: 威曰：「大人清高，不審于何得此絹？

translations.literal: Wei said: 'Father, you are pure and lofty—from where did this silk come?'
translations.idiomatic: Wei asked how a man of such austerity had obtained the silk.

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「是吾俸祿之餘，以為汝糧耳。

translations.literal: Zhi said: 'It is what remains of my salary, meant as provisions for you.'
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi answered that it was leftover salary earmarked for his son's provisions.

sentences.zh: 」威受之，辭歸。

translations.literal: Wei accepted it and took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took it and set out for home.

sentences.zh: 質帳下都督先威未發，請假還家，陰資裝于百餘里，要威為伴，每事佐助。

translations.literal: Before Wei had set out, the commandant [duwei] under Zhi's tent asked leave and returned home, secretly supplied provisions over a hundred li down the road, intercepted Wei as a companion, and assisted him at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wei departed, his father's camp commandant took leave, rode ahead more than a hundred li, stocked supplies in secret, intercepted Wei as a traveling companion, and waited on him at every step.

sentences.zh: 行數百里，威疑而誘問之，既知，乃取所賜絹與都督，謝而遣之。

translations.literal: After several hundred li Wei grew suspicious and questioned him under pretense; once he knew [the truth], he took the silk his father had given him and gave it to the commandant, thanked him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: After several hundred li Wei suspected something, drew the truth out, returned his father's silk to the commandant with thanks, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 後因他信以白質，質杖都督一百，除吏名。

translations.literal: Later, through another messenger, he informed Zhi; Zhi had the commandant flogged one hundred strokes and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote his father; Hu Zhi had the commandant thrashed one hundred strokes and erased him from the roster.

sentences.zh: 其父子清慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus father and son were pure and cautious to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was their mutual purity and care.

sentences.zh: 於是名譽著聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon his reputation spread far.
translations.idiomatic: His name soon traveled widely.

sentences.zh: 拜侍御史，曆南鄉侯、安豐太守，遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Censor, served as Marquis of Nanxiang, Administrator of Anfeng, and was promoted Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He became attendant censor, marquis of Nanxiang, administrator of Anfeng, then inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 勤於政術，風化大行。

translations.literal: He was diligent in governing technique; transforming influence spread broadly.
translations.idiomatic: He worked his administrative craft tirelessly and reshaped local custom.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，武帝語及平生，因歎其父清，謂威曰：「卿孰與父清？

translations.literal: Later he entered court; when Emperor Wu spoke of [his] whole life, he sighed at his father's purity and said to Wei: 'Between you and your father, who is the purer?'
translations.idiomatic: Back at court Emperor Wu reminisced about his life, praised his father's honesty, and asked whether father or son was the cleaner man.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣不如也。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Your servant is not the equal [of his father].'
translations.idiomatic: Wei answered that he could not match his father.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿父以何勝耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'In what does your father surpass you?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked wherein the father excelled.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣父清恐人知，臣清恐人不知，是臣不及遠也。

translations.literal: He replied: 'My father's purity feared that others would know; your servant's purity fears that others would not know—there your servant falls far short.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei said his father's integrity shrank from publicity while his own hungered for recognition—that was how far he fell short.

sentences.zh: 」帝以威言直而婉，謙而順。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Wei's words straightforward yet tactful, modest yet compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found the reply frank yet diplomatic, humble yet loyal.

sentences.zh: 累遷監豫州諸軍事、右將軍、豫州刺史，入為尚書，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervise military affairs in Yu Province with concurrent appointment as General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Province, entered [court] as Masters of Writing, and was additionally given Cavalry Conductor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervise Yu military affairs as General of the Right and inspector of Yu, entered the Masters of Writing, and picked up the additional title cavalry conductor.

sentences.zh: 威嘗諫時政之寬，帝曰：「尚書郎以下，吾無所假借。

translations.literal: Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the Masters of Writing supervisors, I grant no indulgence.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wei complained policy was too soft, Emperor Wu said he showed no mercy below the Masters of Writing tier.

sentences.zh: 」威曰：「臣之所陳，豈在丞郎令史，正謂如臣等輩，始可以肅化明法耳。

translations.literal: Wei said: 'What your servant has stated—how could it concern only assistants and clerks? It is precisely men of your servant's rank who must then be able to stiffen transformation and clarify the law.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied that his point was not about petty clerks—men of his own rank must exemplify discipline so the law shines clear.'

sentences.zh: 」拜前將軍、監青州諸軍事、青州刺史，以功封平春侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Front, supervised military affairs in Qing Province, and became Inspector of Qing Province; for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchun.
translations.idiomatic: He took General of the Front, supervised Qing, served as Qing inspector, and earned the marquisate of Pingchun for merit.

sentences.zh: ，卒於位，追贈使持節、都督青州諸軍事、鎮東將軍，余如故，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died in office. Posthumously he was granted credentials as envoy and concurrently governor of military affairs in Qing Province, General Who Guards the East; his other titles remained as before. His posthumous name was Lie [Ardent].
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. Posthumously he received credentials as commissioner and concurrent governor of Qing military affairs as General Who Guards the East, kept his other honors, and took the posthumous name Lie ('ardent').

sentences.zh: 子奕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 威子 奕

translations.literal: Hu Wei's son Yi
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yi (son of Hu Wei)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Another illustration divider appears here in the transmitted text.

sentences.zh: 奕字次孫，仕至平東將軍。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Cisun, rose to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yi (courtesy Cisun) reached General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 威弟羆，字季象，亦有幹用，仕至益州刺史、安東將軍。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Pi, courtesy name Jixiang, was also capable and effective in office; he rose to Inspector of Yi Province and General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei's younger brother Pi (courtesy Jixiang) was likewise capable, rising to inspector of Yi and General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 杜軫

translations.literal: Du Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen

sentences.zh: 杜軫，字超宗，蜀郡成都人也。

translations.literal: Du Zhen, courtesy name Chaozong, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen (courtesy Chaozong) came from Chengdu in Shu.

sentences.zh: 父雄，綿竹令。

translations.literal: His father Xiong was magistrate of Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Xiong had been magistrate of Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 軫師事譙周，博涉經書。

translations.literal: Zhen studied under Qiao Zhou and broadly read the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen studied under Qiao Zhou and widely explored the classics.

sentences.zh: 州辟不就，為郡功曹史。

translations.literal: The province summoned him but he did not go; he served as clerk of merit for the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial summons he declined; he worked as the commandery clerk of merit.

sentences.zh: 時鄧艾至成都，軫白太守曰：「今大軍來征，必除舊佈新，明府宜避之，此全福之道也。

translations.literal: When Deng Ai arrived at Chengdu, Zhen reported to the Administrator: 'Now the great army has come on campaign—it will surely remove the old and spread the new; you, sir, should withdraw from [office]; that is the way to preserve good fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai entered Chengdu, Du Zhen told the administrator that conquest would sweep away the old order—the wise course was to vacate office and stay safe.

sentences.zh: 」太守乃出。

translations.literal: The Administrator thereupon went out [left office].
translations.idiomatic: The administrator resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 艾果遣其參軍牽弘自之郡，弘問軫前守所在，軫正色對曰：「前守達去就之機，輒自出官舍以俟君子。

translations.literal: Ai indeed sent his adjutant Qian Hong to proceed to the commandery himself; Hong asked Zhen where the former Administrator was, and Zhen answered with stern demeanor: 'The former Administrator grasped the moment to advance or withdraw and left the official residence on his own to await a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai sent adjutant Qian Hong to the commandery; asked where the old administrator had gone, Du Zhen answered coldly that the man had read the times correctly and cleared the yamen to receive an honorable visitor.

sentences.zh: 」弘器之，命復為功曹，軫固辭。

translations.literal: Hong esteemed him and ordered him restored as clerk of merit; Zhen firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hong thought highly of him and tried to put him back in the clerk-of-merit post; Du Zhen refused outright.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，除建寧令，導以德政，風化大行，夷夏悅服。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Jianning; guided by virtuous government, transforming influence spread broadly, and both Yi tribesmen and Han submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Raised as filial and incorrupt, he governed Jianning with benevolent rule until custom changed across the district and every community, tribal or Chinese, accepted his authority.

sentences.zh: 秩滿將歸，群蠻追送，賂遺甚多，軫一無所受，去如初至。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he was about to leave, crowds of Man tribesmen followed him to see him off, offering many bribes and gifts; Zhen accepted nothing and departed as simply as when he had first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: As he finished his tour and prepared to go home, hill peoples trailed after him with lavish parting gifts; he took none of it and rode away as plainly as the day he came.

sentences.zh: 又除池陽令，為雍州十一郡最。

translations.literal: Again appointed magistrate of Chiyang, he ranked first among the eleven commanderies of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His next post was Chiyang, where his evaluation topped all eleven Yong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 百姓生為立祠，得罪者無怨言。

translations.literal: The common people built a shrine to him while he still lived; those sentenced for crimes bore no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Locals raised a shrine to him in his lifetime, and even convicts accepted punishment without grudge.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 軫博聞廣涉，奏議駁論多見施用。

translations.literal: Zhen read widely; his memorials, deliberations, and rebuttals were often put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen was erudite; the court regularly adopted his memorials and policy debates.

sentences.zh: 時涪人李驤亦為尚書郎，與軫齊名，每有論議，朝廷莫能逾之，號蜀有二郎。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xiang of Fu also held the post of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and matched Zhen in reputation; whenever they debated policy the court could not outdo them—they were called the Two Gentlemen of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang of Fu served alongside him as gentleman of the Masters of Writing; their arguments set the standard at court, earning the nickname 'the two gentlemen of Shu.'

sentences.zh: 軫後拜犍為太守，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: Later Zhen was appointed Administrator of Qianwei and enjoyed a strong reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Qianwei and won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 當遷，會病卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: When he was due for promotion he fell ill and died, age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was slated for promotion but died of illness at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 子毗。

translations.literal: His son Pi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Du Pi.

sentences.zh: 軫子 毗

translations.literal: Du Zhen's son Pi
translations.idiomatic: Du Pi (Du Zhen's son)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Another illustration divider in the transmitted text.

sentences.zh: 毗字長基。

translations.literal: Pi, courtesy name Changji.
translations.idiomatic: Du Pi, courtesy Changji.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，成都王穎辟大將軍掾，遷尚書郎，參太傅軍事。

translations.literal: The province raised him as cultivated talent; Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the grand general; he was promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and joined the Grand Tutor's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he entered Prince Chengdu Sima Ying's staff as grand-general aide, then became gentleman of the Masters of Writing and adviser on the grand tutor's army council.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽覆沒，毗南渡江，王敦表為益州刺史，將與宜都太守柳純共固白帝。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell he crossed south of the Yangzi; Wang Dun recommended him as Inspector of Yi Province; he was to cooperate with Administrator of Yidu Liu Chun in holding Ba Di.
translations.idiomatic: After the Luoyang catastrophe he fled south; Wang Dun nominated him for Yi Province so he could join Yidu prefect Liu Chun in defending the Ba gorges.

sentences.zh: 杜弢遣軍要毗，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Du Tao sent troops to intercept Pi; Pi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Du Tao ambushed him and cut him down.

translations.literal: Pi's younger brother Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiu (younger brother of Du Pi)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the source edition.

sentences.zh: 毗弟秀，字彥穎，為羅尚主簿。

translations.literal: Pi's younger brother Xiu, courtesy name Yanying, served as chief clerk to Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiu (courtesy Yanying), Du Pi's younger brother, was chief clerk to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 州沒，為氏賊李驤所得，欲用為司馬。

translations.literal: When the province fell he was captured by the Di leader Li Xiang, who wished to employ him as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After the province collapsed Di warlord Li Xiang seized him and offered him the post of army marshal.

sentences.zh: 秀不受，見害。

translations.literal: Xiu refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiu refused and was executed.

sentences.zh: 毗次子歆，舉秀才。

translations.literal: Pi's second son Xin was raised as cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: Du Pi's second son Du Xin passed the provincial cultivated-talent examination.

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the source edition.

sentences.zh: 軫弟 烈

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Lie
translations.idiomatic: Du Lie (younger brother of Du Zhen)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the source edition.

sentences.zh: 軫弟烈，明政事，察孝廉，曆平康、安陽令，所居有異績，遷衡陽太守。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Lie understood practical administration; recommended as filial and incorrupt, he served as magistrate of Pingkang and Anyang with outstanding records at each post; promoted Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Lie, another brother of Du Zhen, excelled at governance; as filial-and-incorrupt nominee he magistrated Pingkang and Anyang with distinction, then became prefect of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 聞軫亡，因自表兄子幼弱，求去官，詔轉犍為太守，蜀土榮之。

translations.literal: When he heard of Zhen's death he memorialized that his elder brother's sons were still young and weak and begged to resign; an edict transferred him to Administrator of Qianwei; the people of Shu honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Du Zhen's death, he asked leave on the ground that his nephews were infants; the court moved him to Qianwei instead, a gesture Shu folk deeply respected.

sentences.zh: 後遷湘東太守，為成都王穎郎中令，病卒。

translations.literal: Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as palace gentleman to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed eastern Xiang and served as palace gentleman to Prince Chengdu, then died in office of illness.

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the source edition.

sentences.zh: 烈弟 良

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Liang
translations.idiomatic: Du Liang (younger brother of Du Lie)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the source edition.

sentences.zh: 烈弟良，舉秀才，除新都令、涪陵太守，不就，補州大中正，卒。

translations.literal: Liang, younger brother of Lie, was raised as cultivated talent; appointed magistrate of Xindu and Administrator of Fuling—he did not take office; appointed provincial senior evaluator; died.
translations.idiomatic: Du Liang, Du Lie's youngest brother, passed the cultivated-talent exam and received calls to Xindu and Fuling but declined; he ended as the province's senior evaluator and died in that role.

sentences.zh: 竇允

translations.literal: Dou Yun
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yun

sentences.zh: 竇允，字雅，始平人也。

translations.literal: Dou Yun, courtesy name Ya, was a native of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yun (courtesy Ya) came from Shiping.

sentences.zh: 出自寒門，清尚自修。

translations.literal: He came from a humble family and cultivated purity and lofty conduct on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a poor household, he disciplined himself toward austerity and honor.

sentences.zh: 少仕縣，稍遷郡主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he served the county and gradually rose to chief clerk of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He began in county service and worked up to commandery chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，除浩亹長。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Gaomen.
translations.idiomatic: As filial-and-incorrupt nominee he became magistrate of Gaomen county.

sentences.zh: 勤於為政，勸課田蠶，平均調役，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Diligent in governance, he urged farming and sericulture, equalized taxes and corvée; the common people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed farming and silk-rearing, spread levies fairly, and earned the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 遷謁者。

translations.literal: Promoted to usher.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to palace usher.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，詔曰：「當官者能潔身修己，然後在公之節乃全。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era an edict said: 'Those who hold office must purify and cultivate themselves; only then is public integrity complete.
translations.idiomatic: A Taishi edict declared that officials must clean their own conduct before they could serve the state with full honor.'

sentences.zh: 身善有章，雖賤必賞，此興化立教之務也。

translations.literal: When personal goodness is manifest, though the rank be low, reward must follow—this is how one promotes transforming influence and establishes instruction.'
translations.idiomatic: Visible virtue deserves reward even from low station—that is how the court teaches the realm.'

sentences.zh: 謁者竇允前為浩亹長，以修勤清白見稱河右。

translations.literal: Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Gaomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Palace usher Dou Yun had already earned fame west of the Yellow River as a diligent, honest magistrate at Gaomen.'

sentences.zh: 是輩當擢用，使立行者有所勸。

translations.literal: Men of this sort ought to be promoted so that those who practice upright conduct have something to strive toward.
translations.idiomatic: Such men should be lifted up to encourage every upright officer.'

sentences.zh: 主者詳復參訪，有以旌表之。

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices examine and investigate thoroughly and issue commendations.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministries review the facts and give them public recognition.'

sentences.zh: 」拜臨水令。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yun received Linshui county.

sentences.zh: 克己厲俗，改修政事，士庶悅服，咸歌詠之。

translations.literal: He restrained himself and sternly improved custom, revised administration; gentry and commoners submitted gladly and all sang his praises.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened his own conduct, reshaped local practice, and won scholars and farmers alike—they sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 遷钜鹿太守，甚有政績。

translations.literal: Promoted Administrator of Julu; he achieved considerable administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Julu, he compiled a notable administrative record.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 王宏

translations.literal: Wang Hong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong

sentences.zh: 王宏，字正宗，高平人，魏侍中粲之從孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, courtesy name Zhengzong, was a man of Gaoping; he was a collateral descendant of Wang Can, attendant of the inner court in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong (courtesy Zhengzong) of Gaoping traced his line collaterally from Wei inner-court attendant Wang Can.

sentences.zh: 魏時辟公府，累遷尚書郎，曆給事中。

translations.literal: In Wei he was summoned to the ministerial offices; repeatedly promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; served successively as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he entered the central ministries, rose to gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，為汲郡太守，撫百姓如家，耕桑樹藝，屋宇阡陌，莫不躬自教示，曲盡事宜，在郡有殊績。

translations.literal: At the start of Taishi he became Administrator of Ji commandery; he treated the common people like family—plowing, mulberry, planting, houses and field paths—there was nothing he did not personally teach and demonstrate, exhaustively covering what was needful; in the commandery he achieved exceptional results.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he took Ji commandery and treated households like kin: he walked every field and lane to teach sowing, mulberry, and building until nothing essential was left undone, and his ratings soared.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉石鑒上其政術，武帝下詔稱之曰：「朕惟人食之急，而懼天時水旱之運，夙夜警戒，念在於農。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Shi Jian reported his administrative methods; Emperor Wu issued an edict praising him, saying: 'I consider the urgency of people's food and fear the workings of flood and drought in season; day and night I am on guard, my thoughts on agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan governor Shi Jian forwarded his methods; Emperor Wu responded: 'Food is the people's lifeblood; I dread flood and drought and lose sleep over farming.'

sentences.zh: 雖詔書屢下，敕厲殷勤，猶恐百姓廢惰以損生植之功。

translations.literal: Though edicts have been issued repeatedly and instructions earnestly urged, I still fear the common people may grow idle and lazy and impair the work of nurturing growth.'
translations.idiomatic: Edicts rain down and I nag earnestly, yet I worry idleness will still waste the year's growth.'

sentences.zh: 而刺史、二千石、百里長吏未能盡勤，至使地有遺利而人有餘力，每思聞監司糾舉能不，將行其賞罰，以明沮勸。

translations.literal: Yet inspectors, commandery governors of two thousand shi, and magistrates of a hundred li have not been able to do their utmost, so that the land still holds uncultivated surplus while people have leftover strength; whenever I think of this I wish to hear whether overseers report who can and who cannot, so as to apply rewards and punishments and make encouragement and discouragement clear.'
translations.idiomatic: Too many inspectors, prefects, and county magistrates still slack off—fields lie fallow while labor sits idle. I want overseers to name who performs and who fails so rewards and fines can teach the lesson.'

sentences.zh: 今司隸校尉石鑒上汲郡太守王宏勤恤百姓，導化有方，督勸開荒五千餘頃，而熟田常課頃畝不減。

translations.literal: Now Metropolitan Governor Shi Jian reports that Administrator of Ji commandery Wang Hong diligently comforts the common people and guides transformation effectively; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of new fields while tax grain from mature fields did not decrease per mu.'
translations.idiomatic: Now Shi Jian reports that Ji prefect Wang Hong consoles the people and leads them well: he opened over five thousand qing of new land without dropping output on old fields.'

sentences.zh: 比年普饑，人食不足，而宏郡界獨無匱乏，可謂能矣。

translations.literal: In recent years famine has been widespread and people lack food, yet within Hong's commandery alone there was no shortage—this may be called capable.'
translations.idiomatic: Years of famine starved the realm, yet Hong's jurisdiction alone stayed fed—that is real competence.'

sentences.zh: 其賜宏穀千斛，佈告天下，咸使聞知。」

translations.literal: Grant Hong one thousand hu of grain; proclaim this throughout the realm so all may hear and know.'
translations.idiomatic: Award him a thousand hu of grain and broadcast the decree so every circuit hears.'

sentences.zh: 俄遷衛尉、河南尹、大司農，無復能名，更為苛碎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted Commandant of the Guards, Intendant of Henan, and Minister of Agriculture—but he no longer had his former reputation and became harsh and fussy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded the guards, ran Henan, and took the granaries ministry—but the humane magistrate was gone; he turned petty and cruel.

sentences.zh: 坐桎梏罪人，以泥墨塗面，置深坑中，餓不與食，又擅縱五歲刑以下二十一人，為有司所劾。

translations.literal: For putting convicts in cangues, smearing their faces with mud, placing them in deep pits, starving them without food, and furthermore illegally releasing twenty-one persons sentenced to five years or less, he was impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He shackled prisoners, smeared mud on their faces, dropped them in pits, starved them, and illegally freed twenty-one convicts serving five years or less—the ministries impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝以宏累有政績，聽以贖罪論。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Hong had repeatedly had administrative achievements, permitted him to redeem the offense with a fine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor credited his earlier record and let him buy off the charge.

sentences.zh: 太康中，代劉毅為司隸校尉，於是檢察士庶，使車服異制，庶人不得衣紫絳及綺繡錦繢。

translations.literal: In Taikang he replaced Liu Yi as Metropolitan Governor; thereupon he inspected gentry and commoners, making carriage and dress follow different regulations—commoners might not wear purple, crimson, brocade embroidery, or patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang he succeeded Liu Yi as metropolitan governor and regulated dress for nobles and commoners—common people could not wear purple, red, brocade, or figured silk.

sentences.zh: 帝常遣左右微行，觀察風俗，宏緣此復遣吏科檢婦人衵服，至褰發于路。

translations.literal: The emperor often sent attendants incognito to observe customs; Hong on this account again sent clerks to inspect women's under-jackets, to the point of lifting skirts on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign habitually sent plain-clothes agents to gauge morals; Hong sent clerks after women's under-robes and even had garments lifted in the street.

sentences.zh: 論者以為暮年謬妄，由是獲譏於世，復坐免官。

translations.literal: Critics thought him senile and absurd in his later years; on this account he was mocked by the world and again removed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Observers wrote him off as a foolish old man; ridicule followed and he was cashiered again.

sentences.zh: 後起為尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was raised up as Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned as a masters-of-writing minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈太常。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received posthumous appointment as minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 曹攄

translations.literal: Cao Shu
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu

sentences.zh: 曹攄，字顏遠，譙國譙人也。

translations.literal: Cao Shu, courtesy name Yuanyuan, was a native of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu (courtesy Yuanyuan) came from Qiao in the Qiao princedom.

sentences.zh: 祖肇，魏衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao was General Who Guards Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cao Zhao had been Wei general who guards the borders.

sentences.zh: 攄少有孝行，好學善屬文，太尉王衍見而器之，調補臨淄令。

translations.literal: Shu from youth showed filial conduct, loved learning and was skilled at composition; Grand Commandant Wang Yan saw him and esteemed him; he was transferred and appointed magistrate of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Filial from boyhood, bookish and eloquent, he impressed grand commandant Wang Yan, who moved him to magistrate of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 縣有寡婦，養姑甚謹。

translations.literal: In the county was a widow who tended her mother-in-law very carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The county had a widow who nursed her mother-in-law devotedly.

sentences.zh: 姑以其年少，勸令改適，婦守節不移。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law, because she was young, urged her to remarry; the woman kept her chastity and would not move.
translations.idiomatic: The elder, pitying her youth, urged her to remarry; the widow refused to abandon her vow.

sentences.zh: 姑湣之，密自殺。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law pitied her and secretly killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law, heartsick for her, committed suicide in secret.

sentences.zh: 親党告婦殺姑，官為考鞫，寡婦不勝苦楚，乃自誣。

translations.literal: Relatives reported the woman had killed her mother-in-law; officials interrogated her under torture; the widow could not endure the pain and falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Kin accused the widow of murder; torture broke her and she confessed to a crime she did not commit.

sentences.zh: 獄當決，適值攄到。

translations.literal: When the case was to be decided, it happened that Shu arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Sentence was about to fall when Cao Shu took office.

sentences.zh: 攄知其有冤，更加辯究，具得情實，時稱其明。

translations.literal: Shu knew there was injustice and investigated further; he obtained the full truth of the situation; he was at the time praised for his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He sensed a miscarriage, reopened the file, and extracted the truth; contemporaries praised his insight.

sentences.zh: 獄有死囚，歲夕，攄行獄，湣之，曰：「卿等不幸致此非所，如何？

translations.literal: In the jail were condemned prisoners; at year's end Shu inspected the prison and pitied them, saying: 'You have unfortunately come to this place—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's eve he toured death row and said, 'You should not be here—what can be done?'

sentences.zh: 新歲人情所重，豈不欲暫見家邪？

translations.literal: New Year's is what human feelings most treasure—do you not wish briefly to see your families?'
translations.idiomatic: The holiday is when hearts turn home—would you not spend a moment with kin?'

sentences.zh: 」眾囚皆涕泣曰：「若得暫歸，死無恨也。

translations.literal: All the prisoners wept and said: 'If we could return for a little while, we would die without regret.'
translations.idiomatic: They wept that one evening at home would repay any fate.'

sentences.zh: 」攄悉開獄出之，克日令還。

translations.literal: Shu opened all the prisons and released them, setting a deadline for their return.
translations.idiomatic: He threw open the gates, freed them all, and named the day they must return.

sentences.zh: 掾吏固爭，咸謂不可。

translations.literal: The clerks firmly objected, all saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: His aides protested that the risk was insane.

sentences.zh: 攄曰：「此雖小人，義不見負，自為諸君任之。

translations.literal: Shu said: 'Though these are petty men, in honor they will not betray me; I myself answer for them to you gentlemen.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu answered, 'They are humble men but not dishonorable—I alone will answer for them.'

sentences.zh: 」至日，相率而還，並無違者，一縣嘆服，號曰聖君。

translations.literal: When the day came they came back together; none broke the promise—the whole county marveled and submitted, calling him the sage lord.
translations.idiomatic: Every man returned on time; the county hailed him as a sage official.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書郎，轉洛陽令，仁惠明斷，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, transferred to magistrate of Luoyang; benevolent, kind, and clear in judgment—the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the Masters of Writing and then Luoyang county—kind, sharp, and beloved.

sentences.zh: 時天大雨雪，宮門夜失行馬，群官檢察，莫知所在。

translations.literal: At that time heaven sent great rain and snow; at night the traveling barriers at the palace gate were lost; the various officials searched and none knew where they were.
translations.idiomatic: One night of blizzard the palace gate's traveling barriers vanished; no search turned them up.

sentences.zh: 攄使收門士，眾官咸謂不然。

translations.literal: Shu ordered the gate guards seized; all the officials said it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu arrested the gate guards; colleagues called it nonsense.

sentences.zh: 攄曰：「宮掖禁嚴，非外人所敢盜，必是門士以燎寒耳。

translations.literal: Shu said: 'The palace is strictly forbidden—outsiders would not dare steal them; it must be the gate guards taking them to warm themselves by fire.'
translations.idiomatic: He argued the inner palace was impregnable to thieves—the guards must have burned them against the cold.'

sentences.zh: 」詰之，果服。

translations.literal: When questioned, they indeed confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning proved him right.

sentences.zh: 以病去官。

translations.literal: He left office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him out.

sentences.zh: 復為洛陽令。

translations.literal: Again became magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang eventually recalled him.

sentences.zh: 及齊王冏輔政，攄與左思俱為記室督。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong assisted the government, Shu together with Zuo Si both served as supervisors of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi Sima Jiong directed the regime, Cao Shu and Zuo Si jointly supervised the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冏嘗從容問攄曰：「天子為賊臣所逼，莫有能奮。

translations.literal: Jiong once calmly asked Shu: 'The Son of Heaven was coerced by traitorous ministers; none could rouse himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong once asked privately how he should respond now that traitors had seized the emperor and none had stirred.'

sentences.zh: 吾率四海義兵興復王室，今入輔朝廷，匡振時艱，或有勸吾還國，於卿意如何？

translations.literal: I led righteous troops from within the four seas to restore the royal house; now I enter and assist the court, aiding the hardship of the times—some urge me to return to my princedom; what is your thought?'
translations.idiomatic: He had raised armies across the realm to restore Jin and now guided the court—yet voices urged him back to his fief—what did Cao Shu advise?'

sentences.zh: 」攄曰：「蕩平國賊，匡復帝祚，古今人臣之功未有如大王之盛也。

translations.literal: Shu said: 'Sweeping away state rebels and restoring the imperial throne—among ministers through history none has achieved merit as great as the great king's.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu replied that crushing rebels and seating the throne anew was unmatched glory.'

sentences.zh: 然道罔隆而不殺，物無盛而不衰，非唯人事，抑亦天理。

translations.literal: Yet the Way never rises without decline; nothing flourishes without fading—not only in human affairs but also in the pattern of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every zenith tilts toward decline—human affairs mirror heaven's turning wheel.'

sentences.zh: 竊預下問，敢不盡情。

translations.literal: Having received your humble inquiry below, how dare I not speak my whole mind.
translations.idiomatic: Asked for candor, he would withhold nothing.'

sentences.zh: 願大王居高慮危，在盈思沖，精選百官，存公屏欲，舉賢進善，務得其才，然後脂車秣馬，高揖歸籓，則上下同慶，攄等幸甚。

translations.literal: I wish the great king, dwelling high, to think of peril; in fullness to think of emptiness; carefully select the hundred officials; preserve impartiality and restrain desire; promote the worthy and advance the good, striving to obtain true talent—then grease the carriage and feed the horses, bow deeply and return to your fief; then high and low alike will rejoice, and Shu and the rest will be greatly fortunate.'
translations.idiomatic: He begged Jiong to remember danger from the heights and humility in success, pick ministers on merit, stay fair and sober, promote talent—and then retire to his princedom with honor so the realm could rejoice and Cao Shu could rest easy.'

sentences.zh: 」冏不納。

translations.literal: Jiong did not accept the advice.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong brushed the counsel aside.

sentences.zh: 尋轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon moved to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂以為驃騎司馬。

translations.literal: Prince Changsha Sima Yi appointed him marshal for the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changsha Sima Yi named him staff marshal on the agile-cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 乂敗，免官。

translations.literal: When Yi was defeated, [Shu] was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Changsha fell, Cao Shu lost his post.

sentences.zh: 因丁母憂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末，起為襄城太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui's reign he was raised up as Administrator of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Hui's reign he returned as Xiangcheng prefect.

sentences.zh: ，高密王簡鎮襄陽，以攄為征南司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaomi Sima Jian was stationed at Xiangyang and appointed Shu as marshal for the southern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gaomi Sima Jian, commanding Xiangyang, put Cao Shu in charge of the southern army staff.

sentences.zh: 其年流人王逌等聚眾屯冠軍，寇掠城邑。

translations.literal: That year displaced persons led by Wang You and others gathered at Guanjun, raiding towns.
translations.idiomatic: Refugee bands under Wang You encamped at Guanjun that year and looted cities along the way.

sentences.zh: 簡遣參軍崔曠討之，令攄督護曠。

translations.literal: Jian sent adjutant Cui Kuang against them and ordered Shu to supervise Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jian dispatched Cui Kuang to attack them while Cao Shu oversaw Kuang as protector.

sentences.zh: 曠，奸凶人也，譎攄前戰，期為後繼，既而不至。

translations.literal: Kuang was a treacherous man; he tricked Shu into taking the front line, promising reinforcements, then never came.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuang was treacherous: he pushed Cao Shu forward and promised support that never arrived.

sentences.zh: 攄獨與逌戰於酈縣，軍敗死之。

translations.literal: Shu alone fought Wang You at Li county; his force was routed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu met Wang You near Li county alone, lost the battle, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 故吏及百姓並奔喪會葬，號哭即路，如赴父母焉。

translations.literal: Former subordinates and common people alike hurried to mourning and funeral gatherings; they wailed along the road as if burying parents.
translations.idiomatic: Old aides and ordinary folk raced to his funeral, weeping in the street as for a parent.

sentences.zh: 潘京

translations.literal: Pan Jing
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jing

sentences.zh: 潘京，字世長，武陵漢壽人也。

translations.literal: Pan Jing, courtesy name Shichang, was a native of Hanshou in Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jing (courtesy Shichang) came from Hanshou in Wuling commandery.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，郡辟主簿，太守趙廞甚器之，嘗問曰：「貴郡何以名武陵？

translations.literal: At the capping age the commandery summoned him as chief clerk; Administrator Zhao Xin esteemed him highly and once asked: "Why is your commandery called Wuling?"
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age the commandery called him chief clerk. Prefect Zhao Xin favored him and asked why the region bore the name Wuling.

sentences.zh: 」京曰：「鄙郡本名義陵，在辰陽縣界，與夷相接，數為所攻，光武時移東出，遂得全完，共議易號。

translations.literal: Jing replied: "Our commandery was originally Yiling, within Chenyang county; it bordered the Yi tribes and suffered repeated attacks; in Emperor Guangwu's reign it was shifted eastward and survived intact; the elders then chose a new name.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jing explained that the seat had been Yiling on Chenyang's border with tribal neighbors; Guangwu moved it east to safety, and the community renamed it.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰止戈為武，《詩》稱高平曰陵，於是名焉。

translations.literal: The Documents says 'stopping weapons is martial'; the Odes calls a high, peaceful land a "mound"; hence the new name.
translations.idiomatic: The Classics define martial as laying down arms and ling as a serene rise of ground—hence Wuling.

sentences.zh: 」為州所辟，因謁見問策，探得「不孝」字，刺史戲京曰：「辟士為不孝邪？

translations.literal: Summoned by the province, at audience he drew lots for a policy question and received the pair 'unfilial'; the inspector teased Jing: "Are you summoning a man who is unfilial?"
translations.idiomatic: At a provincial audience he drew the lot 'unfilial' during an examination sketch; the inspector joked about recruiting an unfilial son.

sentences.zh: 」京舉版答曰：「今為忠臣，不得復為孝子。

translations.literal: Jing lifted his writing tablet and answered: "Today I am a loyal subject; I cannot also be a filial son."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jing lifted his tablet: a loyal minister cannot always be a model son at home.

sentences.zh: 」其機辯皆此類。

translations.literal: His ready wit was always of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His repartee ran in that vein.

sentences.zh: 後太廟立，州郡皆遣使賀，京白太守曰：「夫太廟立，移神主，應問訊，不應賀。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Ancestral Temple was completed, every province and commandery sent envoys to congratulate; Jing told the administrator: "When the temple is dedicated and spirit tablets move, the court deserves condolence, not cheering.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynastic temple opened, counties sent congratulations; Pan Jing insisted mourners should grieve the move of ancestral tablets, not toast them.

sentences.zh: 」遂遣京作文，使詣京師，以為永式。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Jing compose a memorial and sent it to the capital as the permanent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect had Pan Jing draft the proper notice; Luoyang adopted it as precedent.

sentences.zh: 京仍舉秀才，到洛。

translations.literal: Jing was again raised as cultivated talent and traveled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again as cultivated talent, he went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尚書令樂廣，京州人也，共談累日，深歎其才，謂京曰：「君天才過人，恨不學耳。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing chief Yue Guang, a fellow townsman, talked with him for days, marveled at his gifts, and said: "Your genius surpasses others; I only regret you have not studied.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang of the Masters of Writing, his countryman, debated him for days and sighed that raw genius needed schooling.

sentences.zh: 若學，必為一代談宗。

translations.literal: If you studied, you would surely become this age's master of pure conversation."
translations.idiomatic: With study, he could dominate the fashion for Pure Conversation.

sentences.zh: 」京感其言，遂勤學不倦。

translations.literal: Jing was moved by his words and thereupon studied tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jing took the hint and studied without slackening.

sentences.zh: 時武陵太守戴昌亦善談論，與京共談，京假借之，昌以為不如己，笑而遣之，令過其子若思，京方極其言論。

translations.literal: Administrator Dai Chang of Wuling also loved Pure Talk; when he sparred with Jing, Jing humored him; Chang thought himself superior, laughed him off, and sent him to debate his son Ruosi—only then did Jing unfurl his full argument.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling prefect Dai Chang fancied himself a wit; Pan Jing played dumb until Dai sent him to spar with Dai Yuan—then he revealed his depth.

sentences.zh: 昌竊聽之，乃嘆服曰：「才不可假。

translations.literal: Chang listened in secret and sighed: "Talent cannot be borrowed."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Chang eavesdropped and admitted talent cannot be faked.

sentences.zh: 」遂父子俱屈焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon father and son both conceded.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both yielded the point.

sentences.zh: 曆巴丘、邵陵、泉陵三令。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Baqiu, Shaoling, and Quanling.
translations.idiomatic: He magistrated Baqiu, Shaoling, and Quanling in turn.

sentences.zh: 京明於政術，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: Jing was clear in governing technique; lost goods lay untouched on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: His administration ran so honestly that no one picked up lost property.

sentences.zh: 遷桂林太守，不就，歸家，年五十卒。

translations.literal: Promoted Administrator of Guilin—he did not take office, returned home, and died at fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Called to Guilin, he declined, retired, and died at fifty.

translations.literal: Section heading — Fan Gui (the Wikisource line wraps the surname with editorial markup).
translations.idiomatic: Fan Gui

sentences.zh: -{范}-晷，字彥長，南陽順陽人也。

translations.literal: Fan Gui, courtesy name Yanchang, was a native of Shunyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Gui (courtesy Yanchang) came from Shunyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 少遊學清河，遂徙家僑居。

translations.literal: In youth he studied in Qinghe and then relocated his household there as a sojourner.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in Qinghe as a youth and moved his family there.

sentences.zh: 郡命為五官掾，曆河內郡丞。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him clerk of the five offices; he served as assistant administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery gave him the five-bureaus clerkship; he became assistant administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 太守裴楷雅知之，薦為侍御史。

translations.literal: Administrator Pei Kai esteemed him and recommended him as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Pei Kai admired him and nominated him attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 調補上谷太守，遭喪，不之官。

translations.literal: Transferred to Administrator of Shanggu; he met bereavement and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Shanggu, he stayed home mourning instead.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒左長史，轉馮翊太守，甚有政能，善於綏撫，百姓愛悅之。

translations.literal: Later he became senior clerk of the left to the Minister of Education, transferred to Administrator of Pingyi—very capable in administration, skilled at pacification; the people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to senior clerk under the minister of education, then governed Pingyi with strong relief efforts and popular affection.

sentences.zh: 徵拜少府，出為涼州刺史，轉雍州。

translations.literal: Summoned as Privy Treasurer; went out as Inspector of Liang Province, transferred to Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court called him privy treasurer, then sent him west as Liang inspector and Yong inspector.

sentences.zh: 于時西土荒毀，氏羌蹈藉，田桑失收，百姓困弊，晷傾心化導，勸以農桑，所部甚賴之。

translations.literal: At that time the western regions lay in ruins; Di and Qiang rampaged; harvests failed; the people were desperate; Gui devoted himself to moral suasion, urging farming and silk; his jurisdictions depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest was shattered by Di and Qiang raids and crop failure; Fan Gui preached farming and care until the region stabilized.

sentences.zh: 元康中，加左將軍，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era he was additionally appointed General of the Left and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang he added General of the Left and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 二子：廣、稚。

translations.literal: Two sons: Guang and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Guang and Zhi.
