translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 晷子 廣

translations.literal: Gui's son Guang
translations.idiomatic: Fan Guang (Fan Gui's son)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 廣字仲將。

translations.literal: Guang, courtesy name Zhongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Guang, courtesy Zhongjiang.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除靈壽令，不之官。

translations.literal: Recommended as filial and incorrupt; appointed magistrate of Lingshou—he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended filial and incorrupt for Lingshou, he never took the post.

sentences.zh: 姊適孫氏，早亡，有孫名邁，廣負以南奔，雖盜賊艱急，終不棄之。

translations.literal: His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a grandson Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
translations.idiomatic: His widowed sister had left a grandson, Mai; Fan Guang fled south with the boy on his back and never abandoned him to bandits.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，以為堂邑令。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, exercising interim authority, appointed him magistrate of Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's provisional regime named him magistrate of Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 丞劉榮坐事當死，郡劾以付縣。

translations.literal: Assistant magistrate Liu Rong faced execution for an offense; the commandery impeached him and remanded him to the county.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Liu Rong faced capital charges; the prefect sent him down to the county jail.

sentences.zh: 榮即縣人，家有老母，至節，廣輒聽暫還，榮亦如期而反。

translations.literal: Rong was a local man with an aged mother; at festivals Guang always let him visit home briefly; Rong returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was a local with an elderly mother; Fan Guang released him for holidays and he always returned on time.

sentences.zh: 縣堂為野火所及，榮脫械救火，事畢，還自著械。

translations.literal: The county hall caught fire from a brush blaze; Rong slipped his fetters to fight the fire; when done he locked himself again.
translations.idiomatic: When brush fire threatened the yamen, Liu slipped his chains to fight the flames, then refastened himself.

sentences.zh: 後大旱，米貴，廣散私穀振饑人，至數千斛，遠近流寓歸投之，戶口十倍。

translations.literal: Later came great drought and dear grain; Guang distributed thousands of hu of his private grain to the starving; displaced people flocked in until registered households multiplied tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: During famine he fed thousands of hu from his own granaries; refugees poured in and his county rolls swelled tenfold.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 晷子 稚

translations.literal: Gui's son Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi (Fan Gui's son)

translations.literal: The source line consists of an equals sign, a typographical marker in the edition (often indicating an illustration plate).
translations.idiomatic: Illustration divider in the received text.

sentences.zh: 稚少知名，辟大將軍掾，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhi was known from youth; summoned as aide to the grand general; died young.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi won early fame, joined the grand general's staff, and died young.

sentences.zh: 子汪，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Wang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan Wang has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 丁紹

translations.literal: Ding Shao
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shao

sentences.zh: 丁紹，字叔倫，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Ding Shao, courtesy name Shulun, was a native of the Principality of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shao (courtesy Shulun) came from the Qiao princedom.

sentences.zh: 少開朗公正，早曆清官，為廣平太守，政平訟理，道化大行。

translations.literal: In youth he was open, forthright, and just; early he served in pure posts; as Administrator of Guangping, government was even and lawsuits were clear; transforming guidance spread broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Cheerful and fair in youth, he rose through unsullied posts; at Guangping justice ran straight and instruction spread wide.

sentences.zh: 于時河北騷擾，靡有完邑，而廣平一郡四境乂安，是以皆悅其法而從其令。

translations.literal: At that time north of the Yellow River was in turmoil and no district stood intact, yet Guangping alone enjoyed peace on every border; therefore all rejoiced in his laws and obeyed his commands.
translations.idiomatic: While Hebei burned and every other county shattered, Guangping stayed calm; people welcomed his code.

sentences.zh: 及臨漳被圍，南陽王模窘急，紹率郡兵赴之，模賴以獲全。

translations.literal: When Linzhang was besieged, Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo was desperate; Shao led commandery troops to his rescue; Mo survived thanks to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Linzhang was invested and Prince Nanyang Sima Mo was trapped, Ding Shao marched county troops and saved him.

sentences.zh: 模感紹恩，生為立碑。

translations.literal: Mo, grateful for Shao's kindness, erected a stele for him while Shao still lived.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo was so grateful he raised a stele to Ding Shao during his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州刺史，士庶戀慕，攀附如歸。

translations.literal: Promoted Inspector of Xu Province; gentry and commoners clung to him, attaching themselves as if coming home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Xu inspector, he drew scholars and commoners who clung to him like kin.

sentences.zh: 未之官，復轉荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post he was again transferred Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He never reached Xu—the court shifted him to Jing inspector.

sentences.zh: 從車千乘，南渡河至許。

translations.literal: A train of a thousand carts crossed the Yellow River south to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand-car entourage forded the river toward Xu.

sentences.zh: 時南陽王模為都督，留紹，啟轉為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo was area commander; he detained Shao and petitioned to transfer him to Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Area commander Sima Mo kept him and arranged a Ji inspector posting instead.

sentences.zh: 到鎮，率州兵討破汲桑有功，加甯北將軍、假節、監冀州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his command he led provincial troops, defeated Ji Sang with merit, and was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the North with credentials, supervising Ji military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On station he crushed Ji Sang's bandits and earned General Who Pacifies the North with credentials over Ji.

sentences.zh: 時境內羯賊為患，紹捕而誅之，號為嚴肅，河北人畏而愛之。

translations.literal: At that time Jie bandits plagued the territory; Shao captured and executed them; he was deemed stern; people north of the Yellow River feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted Jie marauders ruthlessly; northerners feared and respected his severity.

sentences.zh: 紹自以為才足為物雄，當官蒞政，每事克舉，視天下之事若運於掌握，遂慨然有董正四海之志矣。

translations.literal: Shao believed his talent could dominate the age; in office he succeeded at every task; seeing all under heaven as moved in his palm, he aspired to reorder the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He fancied himself master of the moment—every policy worked—and dreamed of rectifying the empire.

sentences.zh: 是時王浚盛于幽州，苟晞盛於青州，然紹視二人蔑如也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Jun flourished in Youzhou and Gou Xi flourished in Qingzhou, yet Shao treated both with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun ruled You and Gou Xi ruled Qing, yet Ding Shao sneered at both.

sentences.zh: ，暴疾而卒，臨終歎曰：「此乃天亡冀州，豈吾命哉！

translations.literal: He suddenly died of a violent illness; facing death he sighed: "This is Heaven destroying Ji Province—how could it be my fate alone!"
translations.idiomatic: A violent illness struck him down; dying, he cried that Heaven was killing Ji Province, not merely himself.

sentences.zh: 」懷帝策贈車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai posthumously appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai posthumously named him general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 喬智明

translations.literal: Qiao Zhiming
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhiming

sentences.zh: 喬智明，字元達，鮮卑前部人也。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhiming, courtesy name Yuanda, was a man of the forward division of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhiming (courtesy Yuanda) belonged to the forward wing of the Xianbei confederation.

sentences.zh: 少喪二親，哀毀過禮，長而以德行著稱。

translations.literal: In youth he lost both parents; his grief exceeded ritual propriety; grown, he was famed for virtuous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he mourned beyond ritual and matured renowned for character.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎辟為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying appointed him General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 穎之敗趙王倫也，表智明為殄寇將軍、隆慮、共二縣令。

translations.literal: When Ying defeated Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he memorialized Zhiming as General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong counties.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Prince Zhao Sima Lun, Sima Ying named him General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong.

sentences.zh: 二縣愛之，號為「神君」。

translations.literal: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: Both counties adored him as their "divine official."

sentences.zh: 部人張兌為父報仇，母老單身，有妻無子，智明湣之，停其獄。

translations.literal: A local man Zhang Dui avenged his father; his mother was old and lived alone; he had a wife but no son; Zhiming pitied him and stayed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner Zhang Dui killed for vengeance; his mother lived alone and he lacked an heir; Qiao Zhiming stayed judgment out of mercy.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，令兌將妻入獄，兼陰縱之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he ordered Dui to bring his wife into jail and secretly allowed conjugal visits.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he let Zhang bring his wife into custody and quietly allowed intimacy.

sentences.zh: 人有勸兌逃者，兌曰：「有君如此，吾何忍累之！

translations.literal: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!
translations.idiomatic: Friends urged flight; Zhang refused to shame such a judge.

sentences.zh: 縱吾得免，作何面目視息世間！

translations.literal: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"
translations.idiomatic: Even freedom would leave him unable to show his face.

sentences.zh: 」於獄產一男。

translations.literal: In the jail his wife bore a boy.
translations.idiomatic: His wife delivered a son in prison.

sentences.zh: 會赦，得免。

translations.literal: An amnesty arrived and he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty freed him.

sentences.zh: 其仁感如是。

translations.literal: His humane kindness moved people thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the power of his humane rule.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之伐鄴也，穎以智明為折沖將軍、參丞相前鋒軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Ye, Ying appointed Zhiming General Who Charges the Enemy and adjutant on the prime minister's vanguard staff.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui's expedition against Ye, Sima Ying made him General Who Charges the Enemy on the vanguard staff.

sentences.zh: 智明勸穎奉迎乘輿，穎大怒曰：「卿名曉事，投身事孤。

translations.literal: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Sima Ying to greet the emperor; the prince roared that a clever adviser should not betray him.

sentences.zh: 主上為群小所逼，將加非罪於孤，卿奈何欲使孤束手就刑邪！

translations.literal: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!
translations.idiomatic: Petty men had cornered the throne and would blame the prince—why counsel surrender?

sentences.zh: 共事之義，正若此乎？

translations.literal: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"
translations.idiomatic: Was this loyalty among allies?

sentences.zh: 」智明乃止。

translations.literal: Zhiming thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhiming fell silent.

sentences.zh: 尋屬永嘉之亂，仕于劉曜。

translations.literal: Soon the Yongjia turmoil came; he served Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia chaos erupted he entered Liu Yao's Han-Zhao regime.

sentences.zh: 鄧攸

translations.literal: Deng You
translations.idiomatic: Deng You

sentences.zh: 鄧攸，字伯道，平陽襄陵人也。

translations.literal: Deng You, courtesy name Bodao, was a native of Xiangling in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng You (courtesy Bodao) came from Xiangling in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖殷，亮直強正。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yin was upright, frank, and uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Deng Yin was blunt and incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 鐘會伐蜀，奇其才，自黽池令召為主簿。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui campaigned against Shu, he marveled at his talent and summoned him from magistrate of Mengchi to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's western campaign spotted his talent and pulled him from Mengchi magistrate to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 賈充伐吳，請殷為長史。

translations.literal: When Jia Chong campaigned against Wu, he requested Yin as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's Wu expedition drafted Deng Yin as senior clerk.

sentences.zh: 後授皇太子《詩》，為淮南太守。

translations.literal: Later he instructed the crown prince in the Odes and became Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He tutored the heir apparent in the Classic of Odes and took the Huainan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夢行水邊，見一女子，猛獸自後斷其盤囊。

translations.literal: He dreamed he walked beside water and saw a woman; a fierce beast from behind severed his belt pouch.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of walking waterside: a woman appeared and a beast tore his belt pouch from behind.

sentences.zh: 占者以為水邊有女，汝字也，斷盤囊者，新獸頭代故獸頭也，不作汝陰，當汝南也。

translations.literal: The diviner said: beside water is a woman—that forms the character 'Ru'; severing the belt pouch means a new beast-head replaces the old; you will not go to Runyin but to Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Dream readers said water plus maiden spelled Ru; swapping pouch ornaments meant a new seal—expect Runan, not Runyin.

sentences.zh: 果遷汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Indeed he was transferred Administrator of Runyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Runyin after all.

sentences.zh: 後為中庶子。

translations.literal: Later he became attendant of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant for the heir.

sentences.zh: 攸七歲喪父，尋喪母及祖母，居喪九年，以孝致稱。

translations.literal: You at age seven lost his father; soon after he lost mother and grandmother; observing mourning nine years, he was famed for filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, he buried mother and grandmother in turn and mourned nine years—a model of filial grief.

sentences.zh: 清和平簡，貞正寡欲。

translations.literal: Pure, peaceful, plain and simple; chaste, upright, with few desires.
translations.idiomatic: Calm, modest, and spare in appetite—honest and detached.

sentences.zh: 少孤，與弟同居。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he lived with his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Fatherless early, he kept house with his brother.

sentences.zh: 初，祖父殷有賜官，敕攸受之。

translations.literal: Originally his grandfather Yin had been granted an official patent; an edict ordered You to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yin's ennoblement had passed down by edict to Deng You.

sentences.zh: 後太守勸攸去王官，欲舉為孝廉，攸曰：「先人所賜，不可改也。

translations.literal: Later the administrator urged You to surrender the royal patent so he could be raised as filial and incorrupt; You said: 'What forebears granted cannot be altered.'
translations.idiomatic: The prefect wanted him to yield the inherited title for a filial-and-incorrupt nomination; Deng You refused to dishonor his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 」嘗詣鎮軍賈混，混以人訟事示攸，使決之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he visited General Who Garrisons the Army Jia Hun; Hun showed him a commoner's lawsuit and had him decide it.
translations.idiomatic: At camp commandant Jia Hun's interview he was handed a civil suit to judge.

sentences.zh: 攸不視，曰：「孔子稱聽訟吾猶人也，必也使無訟乎！

translations.literal: You would not look at it and said: 'Confucius said, "In hearing lawsuits I am like others—surely the task is to make lawsuits cease!"'
translations.idiomatic: He declined the brief, quoting Confucius on ending lawsuits rather than judging them.

sentences.zh: 」混奇之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Hun marveled at him and gave him his daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hun admired him and married him to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 舉灼然二品，為吳王文學，曆太子洗馬、東海王越參軍。

translations.literal: Raised in the Zhuoran second-grade category; he became literary instructor to the Prince of Wu; served successively as prince's tutor to the heir, staff to Prince Donghai Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Rated ‘brilliant’ second grade, he taught literature for Prince Wu, tutored the heir, and joined Prince Donghai Sima Yue's staff.

sentences.zh: 越欽其為人，轉為世子文學、吏部郎。

translations.literal: Yue admired his conduct and transferred him to heir's literary instructor and bureau chief in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue esteemed him and moved him to heir's tutor and personnel director.

sentences.zh: 越弟騰為東中郎將，請攸為長史。

translations.literal: Yue's younger brother Teng was General of the Center East and requested You as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng, east-center general, took him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 出為河東太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Hedong.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，沒于石勒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he fell into Shi Le's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia's collapse delivered him to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 然勒宿忌諸官長二千石，聞攸在營，馳召，將殺之。

translations.literal: Yet Le long nursed hatred for officials at two thousand shi; hearing You was in camp, he urgently summoned him intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le despised former prefects; hearing Deng You's rank, he planned execution.

sentences.zh: 攸至門，門幹乃攸為郎時幹，識攸，攸求紙筆作辭。

translations.literal: When You reached the gate, the gate guard had been You's clerk when he was a gentleman; recognizing You, You asked for brush and paper to compose a petition.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate an old clerk recognized him and slipped him brush and paper for a plea.

sentences.zh: 幹候勒和悅，致之。

translations.literal: The clerk waited until Le was mild of mood and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk waited for Shi Le's good humor and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 勒重其辭，乃勿殺。

translations.literal: Le prized his wording and thereupon did not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le admired the prose and spared him.

sentences.zh: 勒長史張賓先與攸比舍，重攸名操，因稱攸於勒。

translations.literal: Le's senior clerk Zhang Bin had formerly lived next door to You and esteemed You's reputation and conduct; thereupon he praised You to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zhang Bin, once his neighbor, praised Deng You until Shi Le listened.

sentences.zh: 勒召至幕下，與語，悅之，以為參軍，給車馬。

translations.literal: Le summoned him to his tent; conversing, he was pleased and appointed him adjutant with carriage and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to HQ, Deng You won a staff post with mounts.

sentences.zh: 勒每東西，置攸車營中。

translations.literal: Whenever Le marched east or west he stationed You's cart in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Every campaign parked Deng You's wagon in headquarters.

sentences.zh: 勒夜禁火，犯之者死。

translations.literal: Le forbade fire by night on pain of death.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le banned night fires on penalty of death.

sentences.zh: 攸與胡鄰轂，胡夜失火燒車。

translations.literal: You camped beside a Hu neighbor; the Hu lost fire by night and burned the carts.
translations.idiomatic: A Hu neighbor's campfire torched the wagon train.

sentences.zh: 吏按問，胡乃誣攸。

translations.literal: Clerks investigated; the Hu then falsely accused You.
translations.idiomatic: Guards questioned the Hu, who blamed Deng You.

sentences.zh: 攸度不可與爭，遂對以弟婦散發溫酒為辭。

translations.literal: You judged he could not contend with them and replied with the excuse that his sister-in-law had loosened her hair warming wine.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing argument was useless, he claimed his sister-in-law had warmed wine by night—a face-saving fiction.

sentences.zh: 勒赦之。

translations.literal: Le pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le accepted the excuse.

sentences.zh: 既而胡人深感，自縛詣勒以明攸，而陰遺攸馬驢，諸胡莫不歎息宗敬之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Hu were deeply moved; they bound themselves and went to Le to clear You, while secretly presenting horses and donkeys to You—all the Hu sighed and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu, ashamed, confessed to Shi Le and sent Deng You livestock; tribesmen revered him.

sentences.zh: 石勒過泗水，攸乃斫壞車，以牛馬負妻子而逃。

translations.literal: When Shi Le crossed the Si River, You broke up his cart and fled carrying wife and children on oxen and horses.
translations.idiomatic: At the Si crossing he smashed the cart and fled with family on draft animals.

sentences.zh: 又遇賊，掠其牛馬，步走，擔其兒及其弟子綏。

translations.literal: Again he met bandits who stripped his oxen and horses; he went on foot, carrying his son and his nephew Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits stole the beasts; he walked, bearing his son and nephew Sui.

sentences.zh: 度不能兩全，乃謂其妻曰：「吾弟早亡，唯有一息，理不可絕，止應自棄我兒耳。

translations.literal: Judging he could not save both, he told his wife: 'My younger brother died early and left only this breath of life—the line cannot end; I must abandon only my own son.'
translations.idiomatic: Unable to save both children, he told his wife his nephew must survive his own boy.

sentences.zh: 幸而得存，我後當有子。

translations.literal: If we are fortunate enough to survive, I shall yet have sons.'
translations.idiomatic: If they lived, he could father another child.

sentences.zh: 」妻泣而從之，乃棄之。

translations.literal: His wife wept and obeyed; thereupon they abandoned [the son].
translations.idiomatic: She wept and consented; they left his son behind.

sentences.zh: 其子朝棄而暮及。

translations.literal: The son abandoned in the morning caught up by evening.
translations.idiomatic: The boy abandoned at dawn somehow reached them by dusk.

sentences.zh: 明日，攸繋之於樹而去。

translations.literal: The next day You tied him to a tree and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Deng You bound his son to a tree and walked on.

sentences.zh: 至新鄭，投李矩。

translations.literal: Reaching Xinzheng he threw himself on Li Ju's protection.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Li Ju at Xinzheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，將去，而矩不聽。

translations.literal: After three years he wished to leave but Ju would not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Li Ju refused his request to leave.

sentences.zh: 荀組以為陳郡、汝南太守，湣帝徵為尚書左丞、長水校尉，皆不果就。

translations.literal: Xun Zu appointed him Administrator of Chen commandery and Runan; Emperor Min summoned him as vice director of the left of the Masters of Writing and colonel of Changshui—none of these posts came to fruition.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial appointments from Xun Zu and Emperor Min never materialized.

sentences.zh: 後密捨矩去，投荀組於許昌，矩深恨焉，久之，乃送家屬還攸。

translations.literal: Later he secretly slipped away from Ju and joined Xun Zu at Xuchang; Ju deeply resented it; after a long while he sent You's family back.
translations.idiomatic: He fled secretly to Xuchang; Li Ju resented it but eventually returned his household.

sentences.zh: 攸與刁協、周顗素厚，遂至江東。

translations.literal: You was always close to Diao Xie and Zhou Yi; he thereupon reached the eastern Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed to the south with Diao Xie and Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 元帝以攸為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him attendant of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him palace aide to the heir.

sentences.zh: 時吳郡闕守，人多欲之，帝以授攸。

translations.literal: At that time Wu commandery lacked an administrator; many coveted it; the emperor gave it to You.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wanted Wu commandery; the throne gave it to Deng You.

sentences.zh: 攸載米之郡，俸祿無所受，唯飲吳水而已。

translations.literal: You shipped grain to the commandery; he accepted no salary—only drank Wu's water.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived carrying grain for relief, took no salary, and drank only local river water.

sentences.zh: 時郡中大饑，攸表振貸，未報，乃輒開倉救之。

translations.literal: At that time the commandery suffered great famine; You memorialized for relief grain; before reply came he opened the granaries and saved the people.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck; before capital approval he opened state granaries.

sentences.zh: 臺遣散騎常侍桓彝、虞慰勞饑人，觀聽善不，乃劾攸以擅出穀。

translations.literal: The court sent imperial household aide Huan Yi and Yu Wei to comfort the starving and observe whether things were well—then impeached You for unauthorized grain issue.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi and Yu Wei inspected the hungry, then impeached him for opening stores.

sentences.zh: 俄而有詔原之。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon absolved him.

sentences.zh: 攸在郡刑政清明，百姓歡悅，為中興良守。

translations.literal: You in the commandery governed with clear punishments and administration; the common people rejoiced; he was a fine administrator of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: His Wu tenure brought lucid justice—acclaimed minister of the restoration.

sentences.zh: 後稱疾去職。

translations.literal: Later he pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Illness became his excuse to resign.

sentences.zh: 郡常有送迎錢數百萬，攸去郡，不受一錢。

translations.literal: The commandery routinely offered several million in send-off and welcome money; when You left the commandery he accepted not one coin.
translations.idiomatic: Locals offered millions in parting gifts; he refused every coin.

sentences.zh: 百姓數千人留牽攸船，不得進，攸乃小停，夜中發去。

translations.literal: Several thousand common people held his boat and would not let it advance; You briefly halted, then slipped away by night.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands gripped his boat until he feigned a stop and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 吳人歌之曰：「紞如打五鼓，雞鳴天欲曙。

translations.literal: The people of Wu sang: "The drum rolls like the fifth watch; the cock crows—dawn nears.
translations.idiomatic: Lines spread along the river: fifth-watch drums and the cock before dawn.

sentences.zh: 鄧侯挽不留，謝令推不去。

translations.literal: Minister Deng cannot be held back; Magistrate Xie cannot be turned away."
translations.idiomatic: They cried that neither Minister Deng nor Magistrate Xie could be refused.

sentences.zh: 」百姓詣臺乞留一歲，不聽。

translations.literal: The common people went to the ministry begging he stay one year; they were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They petitioned the court for one more year; it refused.

sentences.zh: 拜侍中。

translations.literal: He was appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he directed personnel.

sentences.zh: 蔬食弊衣，周急振乏。

translations.literal: He ate vegetables and wore worn clothes; he relieved emergencies and aided the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on greens and rags while aiding the needy.

sentences.zh: 性謙和，善與人交，賓無貴賤，待之若一，而頗敬媚權貴。

translations.literal: By nature modest and agreeable, skilled in dealing with people, he treated guests high or low alike—yet inclined to flatter the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Humble with guests yet currying powerful patrons.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，代周顗為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongchang era he replaced Zhou Yi as General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang era: he succeeded Zhou Yi as guards general.

sentences.zh: ，王敦反，明帝密謀起兵，乃遷攸為會稽太守。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, Ming secretly plotted to raise troops; thereupon he transferred You to Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi plotted against Wang Dun by moving Deng You to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 初，王敦伐都之後，中外兵數每月言之於敦。

translations.literal: Originally, after Wang Dun attacked the capital, inner and outer troop figures were reported to Dun each month.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's coup, monthly troop returns still went to him.

sentences.zh: 攸已出在家，不復知護軍事，有惡攸者，誣攸尚白敦兵數。

translations.literal: You had already left office and no longer knew guards affairs; someone who hated You falsely claimed You still reported troop numbers to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: A foe claimed Deng You still fed Wang Dun troop counts.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而未之信，轉攸為太常。

translations.literal: The emperor heard it but did not believe; he transferred You to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted the tale and moved him to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時帝南郊，攸病不能從。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor performed southern suburb rites; You was ill and could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: During the suburban sacrifice Deng You was too ill to attend.

sentences.zh: 車駕過攸問疾，攸力病出拜。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage passed You's home to inquire after his illness; You forced himself gravely ill to go out and bow.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train stopped at his door; he dragged himself out to bow.

sentences.zh: 有司奏攸不堪行郊而拜道左，坐免。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported You could not perform suburb rites yet bowed beside the road; he was punished by dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him for bowing trackside while skipping the rite—he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 攸每有進退，無喜慍之色。

translations.literal: Whenever You advanced or retreated in office he showed neither joy nor anger.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion or demotion never touched his expression.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted vice director of the right of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became vice president of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，祠以少年。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Minister of the Imperial Household with gold seal and purple ribbon; sacrifice with a young pig.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors included minister of the imperial household, gold seal, purple ribbon, and a pig offering.

sentences.zh: 攸棄子之後，妻子不復孕。

translations.literal: After You abandoned his son, his wife conceived no more.
translations.idiomatic: After abandoning his son his wife bore none.

sentences.zh: 過江，納妾，甚寵之，訊其家屬，說是北人遭亂，憶父母姓名，乃攸之甥。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi he took a concubine whom he favored; questioning her family, she said she was a northerner lost in chaos—recalling parents' names, she was You's niece.
translations.idiomatic: Across the river he favored a concubine who proved, under questioning, to be his niece.

sentences.zh: 攸素有德行，聞之感恨，遂不復畜妾，卒以無嗣。

translations.literal: You had always cultivated virtue; hearing this he was stricken with regret and kept no more concubines; he ended without heir.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, he dismissed concubines and died childless.

sentences.zh: 時人義而哀之，為之語曰：「天道無知，使鄧伯道無兒。

translations.literal: People of the time deemed him righteous and pitied him, saying for him: 'Heaven's way is blind—it left Deng Bodao without sons.'
translations.idiomatic: Popular pity coined the proverb: Heaven left Deng Bodao heirless.

sentences.zh: 」弟子綏服攸喪三年。

translations.literal: His nephew Sui observed mourning for You three years.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Deng Sui mourned him three years.

sentences.zh: 吳隱之

translations.literal: Wu Yin-zhi
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yin-zhi

sentences.zh: 吳隱之，字處默，濮陽鄄城人，魏侍中質六世孫也。

translations.literal: Wu Yin-zhi, courtesy name Chumo, was a man of Juancheng in Puyang; sixth-generation descendant of attendant of the inner court Zhi in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yin-zhi (courtesy Chumo) of Juancheng descended six generations from Wei attendant Wu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 隱之美姿容，善談論，博涉文史，以儒雅標名。

translations.literal: Yin-zhi had handsome features, excelled at discourse, read broadly in literature and history, and was famed for refined scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome, eloquent, learned—known as a Confucian gentleman.

sentences.zh: 弱冠而介立，有清操，雖日晏歠菽，不饗非其粟，儋石無儲，不取非其道。

translations.literal: At the capping age he stood apart with pure conduct: though he supped bean gruel at sunset, he would not eat grain not his own; though he stored not a stone of grain, he would not take by paths unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Young but austere: he starved rather than eat ill-gotten food.

sentences.zh: 年十餘，丁父憂，每號泣，行人為之流涕。

translations.literal: At over ten years he suffered his father's loss; whenever he wailed, passersby wept.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father so loudly strangers wept.

sentences.zh: 事母孝謹，及其執喪，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: Serving his mother he was filial and careful; when observing mourning his grief exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He exceeded ritual mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 家貧，無人鳴鼓，每至哭臨之時，恆有雙鶴警叫，及祥練之夕，復有群雁俱集，時人咸以為孝感所至。

translations.literal: The family was poor and none could beat the drum [for rituals]; whenever they reached the weeping portion of the rites, a pair of cranes always cried aloud; on the nights of xiang and lian ceremonies flocks of geese gathered—all considered it moved by sympathetic resonance.
translations.idiomatic: Poor families lacked funeral drums; cranes and wild geese answered his obsequies—called heaven's echo of his grief.

sentences.zh: 嘗食咸菹，以其味旨，掇而棄之。

translations.literal: Once he ate salted pickles; finding the taste delicious, he picked out and discarded [the pieces].
translations.idiomatic: Tasting savory pickles during mourning, he spat them out for excess pleasure.

sentences.zh: 與太常韓康伯鄰居，康伯母，殷浩之姊，賢明婦人也，每聞隱之哭聲，輟餐投箸，為之悲泣。

translations.literal: He neighbored Minister of Ceremonies Han Kangbo; Kangbo's mother, elder sister of Yin Hao, was a worthy woman; whenever she heard Yin-zhi's weeping she stopped eating and threw down chopsticks, weeping in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kangbo's mother, Yin Hao's sister, wept whenever Wu Yin-zhi wailed next door.

sentences.zh: 既而謂康伯曰：「汝若居銓衡，當舉如此輩人。

translations.literal: Afterward she told Kangbo: 'If you ever hold personnel authority, raise men like this.'
translations.idiomatic: She told her son to promote such men if he ran appointments.

sentences.zh: 」及康伯為吏部尚書，隱之遂階清級，解褐輔國功曹，轉參征虜軍事。

translations.literal: When Kangbo became Minister of Personnel, Yin-zhi thereupon ascended to pure ranks; leaving common cloth he became clerk of merit for General Who Supports the State, transferred to join staff on the campaign against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Kangbo took personnel, Wu Yin-zhi rose from clerk to campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 兄坦之為袁真功曹，真敗，將及禍，隱之詣桓溫，乞代兄命，溫矜而釋之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tan-zhi was clerk of merit to Yuan Zhen; when Zhen fell and disaster threatened, Yin-zhi went to Huan Wen begging to die in his brother's stead; Wen pitied him and released Tan-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his life to Huan Wen to save brother Wu Tan-zhi after Yuan Zhen's fall.

sentences.zh: 遂為溫所知賞，拜奉朝請、尚書郎，累遷晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was known and prized by Wen; appointed court gentleman preparatory, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; repeatedly promoted Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen favored him; he reached Jinling prefect.

sentences.zh: 在郡清儉，妻自負薪。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was pure and frugal; his wife herself carried firewood.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect his wife gathered firewood.

sentences.zh: 入為中書侍郎、國子博士、太子右衛率，轉散騎常侍，領著作郎。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as vice director of the Secretariat, academician of the imperial academy, commander of the heir's right guard; transferred palace attendant and concurrently compiler; promoted General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Central posts stacked up—secretariat, academy, heir's guard, historian, left guard.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝欲用為黃門郎，以隱之貌類簡文帝，乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to make him palace gentleman to the yellow gate but stopped because Yin-zhi resembled Emperor Jianwen in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu cancelled a yellow-gate post fearing he looked like Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 尋守廷尉、秘書監、御史中丞，領著作如故，遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he acted as commandant of justice, director of the Palace Library, censor-in-chief—still concurrent compiler—promoted General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He headed justice, the palace library, and censors while editing histories.

sentences.zh: 雖居清顯，祿賜皆班親族，冬月無被，嘗浣衣，乃披絮，勤苦同於貧庶。

translations.literal: Though occupying eminent purity, he gave stipends to kin; in winter he lacked quilts; he washed his clothes and wore wadding—working as hard as the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He shared salary with relatives and slept under patched cotton like a pauper.

sentences.zh: 廣州包帶山海，珍異所出，一篋之寶，可資數世，然多瘴疫，人情憚焉。

translations.literal: Guangzhou wraps mountains and sea; rare treasures issue forth—a chest of goods can enrich generations—yet miasma abounds and hearts shrink.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou brimmed with pearls but also fever airs men dreaded.

sentences.zh: 唯貧窶不能自立者，求補長史，故前後刺史皆多黷貨。

translations.literal: Only the destitute who could not stand on their own sought staff posts, so former inspectors mostly grew rich from bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Broke men sought the post; predecessors lined their pockets.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲革嶺南之弊，隆安中，以隱之為龍驤將軍、廣州刺史、假節，領平越中郎將。

translations.literal: The court wished to reform Lingnan's abuses; in Long'an it appointed Yin-zhi General Who Rouses the Dragon, Inspector of Guang Province with credentials, concurrent colonel who pacifies the Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Long'an reforms sent Wu Yin-zhi as dragon general and Guangzhou inspector with Yue-pacification colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 未至州二十里，地名石門，有水曰貪泉，飲者懷無厭之欲。

translations.literal: Twenty li short of the provincial seat lies Shimen, where a spring called Greedy Water makes whoever drinks it harbor insatiable desire.
translations.idiomatic: Before the city, Greedy Spring at Shimen was said to inflame covetousness.

sentences.zh: 隱之既至，語其親人曰：「不見可欲，使心不亂。

translations.literal: When Yin-zhi arrived he told his kin: 'Not seeing what can be desired keeps the mind unperturbed.'
translations.idiomatic: He told family that abstaining from temptation steadied the heart.

sentences.zh: 越嶺喪清，吾知之矣。

translations.literal: To lose purity crossing the ranges—I understand how that happens.'
translations.idiomatic: He knew how men spoiled integrity on the frontier.'

sentences.zh: 」乃至泉所，酌而飲之，因賦詩曰：「古人云此水，一歃懷千金。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to the spring, scooped and drank, and composed a poem: "Men of old spoke of this water—one sip loads the breast with desire worth a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: At Greedy Spring he drank deliberately and wrote that one sip could corrupt like gold.

sentences.zh: 試使夷齊飲，終當不易心。

translations.literal: Try offering it to Bo Yi and Shu Qi—they would never change their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Boyi and Shuqi would sip without altering their resolve.'

sentences.zh: 」及在州，清操逾厲，常食不過菜及幹魚而已，帷帳器服皆付外庫，時人頗謂其矯，然亦終始不易。

translations.literal: While in the province his pure conduct grew sterner; ordinarily he ate nothing beyond vegetables and dried fish; curtains, utensils, and clothing all went to the outer treasury—people thought him affected, yet from first to last he never altered.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he tightened austerity—greens and dried fish, gear warehoused—critics called him theatrical but he never wavered.

sentences.zh: 帳下人進魚，每剔去骨存肉，隱之覺其用意，罰而黜焉。

translations.literal: Camp followers presented fish, always boning out meat; Yin-zhi perceived their intent and fined and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: When aides served deboned fish to curry favor, he cashiered them.

sentences.zh: 元興初，詔曰：「夫孝行篤於閨門，清節厲乎風霜，實立人之所難，而君子之美致也。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanxing an edict said: "Filial conduct rooted in inner chambers, pure integrity tempered by frost and wind—such things are truly hard for ordinary men yet mark the finest gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: A Yuanxing edict praised household virtue and frost-proof integrity as rare gentlemanly feats.'

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍、廣州刺史吳隱之孝友過人，祿均九族，菲己潔素，儉愈魚飧。

translations.literal: General Who Rouses the Dragon, Inspector of Guangzhou Wu Yin-zhi surpasses others in filial devotion and friendship, divides stipends among nine branches of kin, keeps himself spare and pure, more frugal than a meal of fish alone.
translations.idiomatic: It cited Wu Yin-zhi's filial generosity, equal stipends for kin, and diet poorer than a fish supper.'

sentences.zh: 夫處可欲之地，而能不改其操，饗惟錯之富，而家人不易其服，革奢務嗇，南域改觀，朕有嘉焉。

translations.literal: Standing where desire could strike yet not changing his integrity; facing piled riches yet his household changes not its clothing—rejecting extravagance for thrift, he altered southern outlook—I approve.
translations.idiomatic: Tempted by Guangzhou's wealth yet unmoved, family still in coarse cloth—his thrift reshaped the Lingnan frontier.'

sentences.zh: 可進號前將軍，賜錢五十萬、穀千斛。」

translations.literal: He may advance to General of the Front; grant fifty myriad cash and one thousand hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Promote him general of the front with cash and grain awards.'

sentences.zh: 及盧循寇南海，隱之率厲將士，固守彌時，長子曠之戰沒。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun raided Nanhai, Yin-zhi rallied officers and soldiers and held firm for a long time; his eldest son Kuang-zhi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun struck Guangzhou; Wu Yin-zhi held the walls until his heir Wu Kuang-zhi fell.

sentences.zh: 循攻擊百有餘日，逾城放火，焚燒三千餘家，死者萬餘人，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Xun attacked over a hundred days, crossed the walls with fire, burned more than three thousand households—over ten thousand dead—and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: After a hundred-day siege Lu Xun fired the suburbs, killing tens of thousands before the city collapsed.

sentences.zh: 隱之攜家累出，欲奔還都，為循所得。

translations.literal: Yin-zhi brought his household out, wished to flee back to the capital, and was captured by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yin-zhi fled with family toward Jiankang but Lu Xun seized them.

sentences.zh: 循表朝廷，以隱之党附桓玄，宜加裁戮，詔不許。

translations.literal: Xun memorialized the court that Yin-zhi had attached to Huan Xuan and should be executed; an edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun accused him of siding with Huan Xuan; the court refused execution.

sentences.zh: 劉裕與循書，令遣隱之還，久方得反。

translations.literal: Liu Yu wrote Xun ordering Yin-zhi returned; only after a long interval did he come back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu demanded his release; months passed before he sailed home.

sentences.zh: 歸舟之日，裝無餘資。

translations.literal: On the day his boat turned homeward his baggage held no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His return junk carried no private fortune.

sentences.zh: 及至，數畝小宅，籬垣仄陋，內外茅屋六間，不容妻子。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he had a small compound of several mu; hedges narrow and cramped; six thatched rooms inside and out—not enough space for wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Home was a few acres of hut—six thatched rooms too tight for his household.

sentences.zh: 劉裕賜車牛，更為起宅，固辭。

translations.literal: Liu Yu gifted carriage and oxen and offered to build him a dwelling; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu offered ox-cart and a new house; Wu Yin-zhi refused.

sentences.zh: 尋拜度支尚書、太常，以竹篷為屏風，坐無氈席。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonies—bamboo blinds served as screens; he sat without felt mats.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of finance and rites he screened rooms with bamboo mats and sat on bare boards.

sentences.zh: 後遷中領軍，清儉不革，每月初得祿，裁留身糧，其餘悉分振親族，家人績紡以供朝夕。

translations.literal: Later promoted central protector of the army—pure frugality unchanged; each month when stipend arrived he retained only personal grain and divided the rest among kin; the household spun and wove for daily meals.
translations.idiomatic: Central guard commander pay still fed relatives after he skimmed daily rice; women spun for food.

sentences.zh: 時有困絕，或並日而食，身恆布衣不完，妻子不沾寸祿。

translations.literal: Sometimes utterly destitute, sometimes eating every other day; his person always wore incomplete cloth; wife and children received none of his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Days brought doubled hunger and patched robes—family saw none of his salary.

sentences.zh: ，請老致事，優詔許之，授光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，賜錢十萬、米三百斛。

translations.literal: He petitioned to retire on grounds of age; a gracious edict permitted it; he was awarded Minister of the Imperial Household with gold seal and purple ribbon, granted one hundred thousand cash and three hundred hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Old age retirement brought minister of the imperial household honors, purple ribbon, cash, and rice.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; posthumously awarded vice minister of the imperial household with concurrent imperial household aide.
translations.idiomatic: He died Yixi year nine with posthumous vice minister and attendant honors.

sentences.zh: 隱之清操不渝，屢被褒飾，致事及於身沒，常蒙優錫顯贈，廉士以為榮。

translations.literal: Yin-zhi's pure conduct never wavered; repeatedly he received imperial praise; from retirement through death he constantly enjoyed generous gifts—men of integrity counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: Honors followed him from resignation through death—clean officials prized the recognition.

sentences.zh: 初，隱之為奉朝請，謝石請為衛將軍主簿。

translations.literal: Originally when Yin-zhi was court gentleman preparatory, Xie Shi requested him as chief clerk to General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yin-zhi was court gentleman, Xie Shi recruited him for the guards general's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隱之將嫁女，石知其貧素，遣女必當率薄，乃令移廚帳助其經營。

translations.literal: When Yin-zhi was about to marry off his daughter, Shi knew his poverty and plainness—that a send-off must be meager—thereupon ordered kitchen and tent moved to assist preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the wedding would be bare, Xie Shi shipped kitchens and tents to help.

sentences.zh: 使者至，方見婢牽犬賣之，此外蕭然無辦。

translations.literal: When the messenger arrived he saw only a maid leading a dog to sell—beyond that nothing whatsoever had been prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys found only a maidservant selling a dog—nothing else ready.

sentences.zh: 後至自番禺，其妻劉氏齎沈香一斤，隱之見之，遂投於湖亭之水。

translations.literal: Later returning from Panyu, his wife Liu carried one jin of aloeswood; Yin-zhi seeing it threw it into Lake pavilion waters.
translations.idiomatic: His wife brought aloeswood from Guangzhou; he dumped it into the lake kiosk.

sentences.zh: 子延之復厲清操，為鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: Son Yan-zhi likewise upheld pure conduct; became Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Son Wu Yan-zhi governed Poyang with equal austerity.

sentences.zh: 延之弟及子為郡縣者，常以廉慎為門法，雖才學不逮隱之，而孝悌潔敬猶為不替。

translations.literal: Yan-zhi's younger brothers and sons who served in commanderies and counties always took integrity and caution as house rule; though talent did not match Yin-zhi's, filial piety, brotherliness, purity, and reverence did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Younger kin in county office inherited his cautious integrity—less gifted but equally dutiful.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: 【Historical Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魯芝等建旟剖竹，布政宣條，存樹威恩，沒留遺愛，咸見知明主，流譽當年。

translations.literal: The historians say: Lu Zhi and the others unfurled command banners and wielded split bamboo tallies, spread governance and proclaimed ordinances; alive they planted awe and kindness, dead they left lingering love—all were recognized by enlightened sovereigns and enjoyed praise in their own day.
translations.idiomatic: The editors praise these prefects for governance that won both sovereigns and commoners.

sentences.zh: 若伯武之潔己克勤，顏遠之申冤緩獄，鄧攸贏糧以述職，吳隱酌水以厲精，晉代良能，此焉為最。

translations.literal: Such as Bowu's purifying himself and mastering diligence, Yuanyuan's rectifying wrongs and easing prisons, Deng You bearing grain to office, Wu Yin-zhi scooping water to steel his essence—among Jin administrators these were the ablest.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei, Cao Shu, Deng You, and Wu Yin-zhi epitomized Jin integrity.

sentences.zh: 而攸棄子存侄，以義斷恩，若力所不能，自可割情忍痛，何至預加徽纆，絕其奔走者乎！

translations.literal: Yet You abandoned his son to preserve his nephew, severing affection by righteousness—if strength truly failed, one might cut feeling and endure pain—why beforehand bind him with fetters and cut off one who would run to help!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Deng You tying his son abandoned kinship—if fate forced choice, why bind the boy to a tree?

sentences.zh: 斯豈慈父仁人之所用心也？

translations.literal: Could this be what loving fathers and humane men intend in their hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Would a humane father act so?

sentences.zh: 卒以絕嗣，宜哉！

translations.literal: Ending without heirs—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Childlessness suited such choices.

sentences.zh: 勿謂天道無知，此乃有知矣。

translations.literal: Say not Heaven's way is blind—here Heaven plainly sees.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven noticed.

sentences.zh: 世英盡節曹氏，犯門斬關，宣帝收雷霆之威，獎忠貞之烈，豈非既已在我，欲其罵人者歟！

translations.literal: Shiying exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; the Emperor Xuan unleashed thunderbolt wrath yet rewarded steadfast martyrdom—is it not that once mastery rested with him, he desired men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi stayed loyal to Wei; Sima Yi spared him—perhaps victors still needed moral examples.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：猗歟良宰，嗣美前賢。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Ah, worthy magistrates—carrying forward the beauty of earlier sages.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: noble ministers inheriting ancient virtue.

sentences.zh: 威同禦黠，靜若烹鮮。

translations.literal: Awesome alike in resisting craftiness, tranquil as cooking a small fish.
translations.idiomatic: They daunted knaves and ruled lightly, like frying small fish.

sentences.zh: 唯嘗吳水，但挹貪泉。

translations.literal: Some tasted only Wu water; others scooped only the Greedy Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Some drank Suzhou river water; others drank Greedy Spring on purpose.

sentences.zh: 人風既偃，俗化斯遷。

translations.literal: Once exemplary conduct bends the way, vulgar custom shifts in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When exemplars bow, folkways follow.
